<!-- ==========================================================================
     WHAT THIS DOCUMENT DOES

     Single-molecule (DAF-seq / Fiber-seq style) analysis of nucleosome
     footprints, MSPs and TF footprints called by fiberHMM v2.9.7, at six
     enhancers, comparing DMSO vs dTag (TWIST1 degron, SNAI1/2 degron).

     Per enhancer it produces:
       1. a read-level "heatmap" of nucleosome footprints, k-means clustered
          on the local nucleosome pattern, with an ATAC track and DMSO->dTag
          cluster-flow ribbons;
       2. a log2(dTag/DMSO) bar panel of the % of reads in each cluster;
       3. an open/closed summary log2FC, where "open" clusters are defined
          automatically from MSP geometry around the motif;
       4. TF-footprint occupancy metaplots (all reads vs accessible reads);
       5. a cross-enhancer summary and a CMH-tested TF occupancy barplot.

     STRUCTURE
       Section 1  CONFIGURATION  <-- the ONLY place with absolute paths
       Section 2  Libraries
       Section 3  Enhancer registry (names, coordinates, motifs, k, clusters)
       Section 4  Sample / file-path helpers
       Section 5  Core functions
       Section 6  Per-enhancer analyses
       Section 7  Cross-enhancer summaries
     ========================================================================== -->


# 1. Configuration

     >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  THE ONLY PLACE WITH ABSOLUTE PATHS  <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<

     Before pushing to GitHub, replace the four strings below with relative
     paths or environment lookups, e.g.

         DAF_ROOT <- Sys.getenv("DAF_ROOT", "data/fiberHMM")
         ATAC_DIR <- Sys.getenv("ATAC_DIR", "data/atac")
         FIG_DIR  <- "figures"
         ROBJ_DIR <- "cache"

     Nothing else in this document contains a machine-specific path.
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r config}
## ---- paths -----------------------------------------------------------------
DAF_ROOT <- "/Volumes/storage/DAFseq/DAFseq_pacbio_exp2_andplasmid_fiber/DAF_QC_marlowe"
ATAC_DIR <- file.path("/Users/luciaichino/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox",
                      "lucia (1)/Lucia 09_05_16/postdoc/Wysocka_lab_personal_folder",
                      "seq_data/dataforIGV")
FIG_DIR  <- file.path("/Users/luciaichino/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox",
                      "lucia (1)/Lucia 09_05_16/postdoc/Wysocka_lab_personal_folder",
                      "SNAI_paper/codes/single molecule/DAF/figures_min1")
ROBJ_DIR <- file.path(FIG_DIR, "min1Robj")

## ---- run options -----------------------------------------------------------
FIBERHMM_VER <- "fiberHMM_v2.9.7"

# TRUE  = recompute bundles + k-means and overwrite the cache
# FALSE = reuse cached .rds where present

REBUILD_CLUSTERS <- TRUE

## ---- k-means -----------------------------------------------------------
# kmeans(centers = <k>) seeds by SAMPLING ROWS, so the
# result depends on the order the bundles happen to be stacked in. Rows are now
# sorted into a canonical, locale-independent order before clustering, and the
# search is run much harder, so a run is reproducible from (reads, k, seed)
# alone.
KMEANS_SEED      <- 42L
KMEANS_NSTART    <- 200L   # was 25 -- see C7 for why 25 was not enough
KMEANS_ITER_MAX  <- 200L
# Full-data k-means at nstart = 200 is impractical here (~180k reads x ~400 bp
# per start). Instead the many random starts are run on a subsample to find
# good centres, then ONE deterministic pass over all reads refines them from
# those centres. Set to NULL to run every start on the full matrix.
KMEANS_SUBSAMPLE <- 20000L

## ---- analysis choices ------------------------------------------------------
TF_SCORE_THR <- 70L    # blockTq quality floor for TF footprints
TF_MAX_WIDTH <- 40L    # drop TF "footprints" wider than this (nucleosome-scale)
MIN_READ_COV <- 5L     # bp with fewer spanning reads than this are NA

LOW_COV_RULE <- "both"

MIN_READS_FC      <- 30L
MIN_READS_FC_ENH1 <- 110L

dir.create(FIG_DIR,  recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(ROBJ_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

fig  <- function(...) file.path(FIG_DIR,  ...)   # figure output path
robj <- function(...) file.path(ROBJ_DIR, ...)   # cached object path

# null-coalescing operator (base R only has it from 4.4.0)
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
```

# 2. Libraries

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)      # dplyr / tidyr / purrr / stringr / ggplot2 / readr
library(GenomicRanges)
library(rtracklayer)    # import.bw() for the ATAC tracks
library(patchwork)      # p1 | p2 composition
library(ggpubr)         # ggarrange();  FIX B7: was loaded mid-document
library(ggnewscale)     # second fill scale for the motif bands
library(ggrastr)        # rasterise the dense footprint rectangles
library(zoo)            # rollmean() in the midpoint metaplot
library(scales)         # comma(), pretty_breaks()

# fiberHMM writes very long BED lines (one block per footprint per read).
# Only relevant if a file is ever handed to readr as a *connection*.
Sys.setenv(VROOM_CONNECTION_SIZE = 500072)

# ---- conflicted -------------------------------------------------------------
# tidyverse + Bioconductor collide on a lot of common verb names (filter, lag,
# rename, select, slice, first, last, reduce, expand, the set operations...).
# Ambiguous calls in this document are namespaced explicitly, but if the
# `conflicted` package is attached these preferences settle the rest up front
# rather than letting them surface one error at a time mid-run.
if (requireNamespace("conflicted", quietly = TRUE) &&
    "conflicted" %in% loadedNamespaces()) {
  prefer <- function(pkg, fn) {
    try(conflicted::conflict_prefer(fn, pkg, quiet = TRUE), silent = TRUE)
  }
  for (f in c("filter", "lag", "select", "rename", "slice", "mutate", "count",
              "first", "last", "desc", "collapse", "summarise", "n")) prefer("dplyr", f)
  for (f in c("expand", "unnest", "complete", "extract"))              prefer("tidyr", f)
  for (f in c("map", "reduce", "discard", "compact", "simplify"))      prefer("purrr", f)
  for (f in c("setdiff", "intersect", "union", "setequal"))            prefer("base",  f)
  rm(prefer, f)
}
```

# 3. Enhancer registry

<!-- ==========================================================================
     One row per analysed window. `label` is the ONLY name that reaches a
     figure. Everything else in the document refers to enhancers by their
     internal key and calls enh_label() to render the name.

     `cluster_range` selects which reads enter the k-means and defines the
     matrix columns. `plot_range` is the (wider) window that gets drawn.
     `minset`        is the fiberHMM call set used -- see reviewer note Q1.
     `accessible`    are the cluster IDs treated as "open" in the TF
                     occupancy quantification (post-hoc, from the metaplots).
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r enhancer-registry}
# ---- accessors -------------------------------------------------------------
# enh_label("enh10")           -> "Enh 2"
# enh_label("enh10", "peak 1") -> "Enh 2 peak 1"
enh_label <- function(key, suffix = NULL) {
  lab <- ENH[[key]]$label
  if (is.null(lab)) stop("No registry entry for enhancer key '", key, "'")
  if (is.null(suffix)) lab else paste(lab, suffix)
}

# "enh10" -> "Enh2"; used to build output filenames from the paper name so the
# PDFs on disk can no longer disagree with the titles inside them.
enh_slug <- function(key, suffix = NULL) {
  s <- gsub(" ", "", ENH[[key]]$label)
  if (is.null(suffix)) s else paste0(s, "_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "", suffix))
}

# fig_name("enh10", "heatmap", "peak1") -> <FIG_DIR>/Enh2_peak1_heatmap_v297.pdf
fig_name <- function(key, what, suffix = NULL, ext = "pdf") {
  fig(paste0(enh_slug(key, suffix), "_", what, "_v297.", ext))
}

# GRanges built from the registry, so chrom can never drift from coordinates
enh_gr <- function(key, which = c("cluster", "plot", "tf_plot", "atac_plot"),
                   peak = NULL) {
  which <- match.arg(which)
  cfg   <- ENH[[key]]
  ir    <- if (!is.null(peak) && !is.null(cfg$peaks[[peak]][[which]])) {
    cfg$peaks[[peak]][[which]]
  } else if (!is.null(cfg[[which]])) {
    cfg[[which]]
  } else {
    cfg$plot     # sensible fallback: tf_plot/atac_plot default to plot
  }
  GRanges(cfg$chrom, ir)
}

# Accessible ("open") cluster IDs, per enhancer or per peak.
#
# WHY THIS IS A FUNCTION AND NOT A BARE $accessible LOOKUP:
# compute_tf_metaplot(clusters = NULL) applies NO cluster filter and returns
# the all-reads curve. So a missing or mistyped `accessible` would not error --
# it would quietly draw every read under an "accessible reads" title. Erroring
# here makes that impossible.
enh_accessible <- function(key, peak = NULL) {
  cfg <- ENH[[key]]
  if (is.null(cfg)) stop("No registry entry for enhancer key '", key, "'")
  a <- if (!is.null(peak)) cfg$peaks[[peak]]$accessible else cfg$accessible
  if (is.null(a) || length(a) == 0) {
    stop("No `accessible` cluster set for '", key,
         if (!is.null(peak)) paste0("' peak '", peak, "'") else "'",
         "`. Enhancers clustered per peak (e.g. enh10) require the `peak` ",
         "argument, because cluster 1 means a different thing in each ",
         "clustering. Returning NULL here would silently pool EVERY cluster.")
  }
  as.character(a)
}

# motif band table for the plotting helpers
enh_motifs <- function(key, set = c("motifs", "motifs_tf"), peak = NULL) {
  set <- match.arg(set)
  cfg <- ENH[[key]]
  if (!is.null(peak) && !is.null(cfg$peaks[[peak]]$motifs)) return(cfg$peaks[[peak]]$motifs)
  if (!is.null(cfg[[set]])) return(cfg[[set]])
  cfg$motifs
}
```

# 4. Samples and file paths

```{r sample-helpers}
# ---- short sample name  <->  on-disk directory stem -------------------------
# "SNAI_rep1_DMSO5min"  ->  "SNAI1FVSNAI2KO_rep1_DMSO5min"
# "TWIST1_rep1_DMSO5min"->  "TWIST1FV_rep1_DMSO5min"
SAMPLE_PREFIX <- c(SNAI = "SNAI1FVSNAI2KO", TWIST1 = "TWIST1FV")

sample_stem <- function(samples) {
  tf   <- sub("_.*$", "", samples)
  rest <- sub("^[^_]+_", "", samples)
  unname(paste0(SAMPLE_PREFIX[tf], "_", rest))
}

# ---- canonical sample vectors ----------------------------------------------
SNAI_SAMPLES <- c(
  "SNAI_rep1_DMSO5min", "SNAI_rep1_dTag5min",
  "SNAI_rep2_DMSO5min", "SNAI_rep2_dTag5min",
  "SNAI_rep1_DMSO1min", "SNAI_rep1_dTag1min",
  "SNAI_rep2_DMSO1min", "SNAI_rep2_dTag1min"
)
TWIST1_SAMPLES <- sub("^SNAI", "TWIST1", SNAI_SAMPLES)
BOTH_SAMPLES   <- c(SNAI_SAMPLES, TWIST1_SAMPLES)

only <- function(samples, pattern) grep(pattern, samples, value = TRUE)

# ---- fiberHMM .bed path builder --------------------------------------------
# kind: "footprint" (nucleosomes), "tf" (TF footprints), "msp" (accessible patches)
daf_bed <- function(samples, minset, kind = c("footprint", "tf", "msp")) {
  kind <- match.arg(kind)
  stem <- sample_stem(samples)
  setNames(
    file.path(DAF_ROOT, minset, "results", stem, FIBERHMM_VER,
              paste0(stem, ".recalled_", kind, ".bed")),
    samples
  )
}

# convenience: the file set an enhancer needs, using ITS minset (see Q1)
enh_files <- function(key, samples, kind = "footprint") {
  daf_bed(samples, ENH[[key]]$minset, kind)
}

# ---- bulk ATAC bigWigs ------------------------------------------------------
ATAC_BW <- c(
  SNAI_DMSO   = file.path(ATAC_DIR, "ATAC_DMSO_merged.bw"),
  SNAI_dTag   = file.path(ATAC_DIR, "ATAC_3h_merged.bw"),
  TWIST1_DMSO = file.path(ATAC_DIR, "GSM7213525_TWIST1FV_dTAG0h_r1_ATAC.bw"),
  TWIST1_dTag = file.path(ATAC_DIR, "GSM7213526_TWIST1FV_dTAG3h_r1_ATAC.bw")
)

# map merged pseudo-sample names -> the right bigWig
atac_for <- function(merged_samples) {
  key <- paste0(ifelse(grepl("TWIST1", merged_samples), "TWIST1", "SNAI"), "_",
                ifelse(grepl("DMSO",   merged_samples), "DMSO",   "dTag"))
  setNames(unname(ATAC_BW[key]), merged_samples)
}

# ---- replicate merging ------------------------------------------------------
# "SNAI_rep1_DMSO5min" -> group "SNAI_DMSO_5min"
# Generated, never typed, so the merged names can never drift between sections.
merged_name <- function(samples) {
  tf   <- ifelse(grepl("^TWIST1", samples), "TWIST1", "SNAI")
  trt  <- ifelse(grepl("DMSO",    samples), "DMSO",   "dTag")
  time <- stringr::str_extract(samples, "\\d+min")
  paste(tf, trt, time, sep = "_")
}
merge_groups_for <- function(samples) split(samples, merged_name(samples))

# ---- palettes ---------------------------------------------------------------
twist_palette <- c("#08519c", "#6baed6")   # dark blue,  light blue
snai_palette  <- c("#a50f15", "#fc8d59")   # dark red,   light red

TF_FILL <- c(TWIST1 = "darkblue", SNAI = "darkred")   # read-rectangle colours

META_COLORS <- c(                                     # metaplot line colours
  TWIST1_DMSO = "#56B4E9", TWIST1_dTag = "#CC79A7",
  SNAI_DMSO   = "#99000D", SNAI_dTag   = "#FC9272"
)

# shared geometry for every linked heatmap, so the panels are comparable
LINKED_STYLE <- list(
  raster_dpi = 300, cluster_gap = 0.8, binding_site_linewidth = 0.4,
  lane_height = 180, atac_gap = 5, atac_height = 10,
  label_gap = 5, label_tier_gap = 8,
  sample_label_gap = 7, group_label_gap = 14
)

# ---- caching ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Replaces the old saveRDS(x, f); x <- readRDS(f) pattern (see C2).
cache_rds <- function(name, expr, rebuild = REBUILD_CLUSTERS) {
  f <- robj(paste0(name, ".rds"))
  if (!rebuild && file.exists(f)) {
    message("cache hit : ", basename(f))
    return(readRDS(f))
  }
  message("computing : ", basename(f))
  val <- force(expr)
  saveRDS(val, f)
  val
}
```

# 5. Core functions

## 5.1 Reading fiberHMM BED files

<!-- ==========================================================================
     fiberHMM writes one BED12-like line per READ, with one block per
     footprint. Two flavours appear in this project:

       13 columns : nucleosome footprint and MSP files (v2.9.7). Column 13 is
                    blockRgb.
       15 columns : TF footprint files. Columns 13-15 are blockTq / blockEl /
                    blockEr, where blockTq is the per-footprint quality byte
                    of fiberHMM's tf.QQQ annotation. blockEl / blockEr are
                    edge-sharpness bytes, NOT quality -- the score filter must
                    use blockTq.

     WHY NOT rtracklayer::import(): its BED/bigBed parser tries to coerce the
     list-valued extra columns to a single integer and fails. We parse as
     plain text instead.
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r fn-read-bed}
# 13-column layout (nucleosome / MSP files)
BED_COLS_13 <- c("chrom", "chromStart", "chromEnd", "name", "score", "strand",
                 "thickStart", "thickEnd", "itemRgb", "blockCount",
                 "blockSizes", "chromStarts", "blockRgb")

# 15-column layout (TF footprint files)
BED_COLS_15 <- c("chrom", "chromStart", "chromEnd", "name", "score", "strand",
                 "thickStart", "thickEnd", "itemRgb", "blockCount",
                 "blockSizes", "chromStarts", "blockTq", "blockEl", "blockEr")

#' Parse one fiberHMM .bed into reads + footprints
#'
#' @return list(reads, footprints)
#'   reads      : chrom, read_name, read_start, read_end, read_score, strand
#'   footprints : chrom, read_name, fp_start, fp_end, fp_width [, blockTq]
#'
#' COORDINATES: BED is 0-based half-open. Both tables are returned 1-based
#' inclusive, so a footprint of width w has fp_end - fp_start + 1 == w.
read_fiberhmm_bed <- function(path) {

  lines    <- read_lines(path)
  n_fields <- str_count(lines, "\t") + 1L

  # Auto-detect the layout from the modal field count.
  expected <- as.integer(names(which.max(table(n_fields))))
  if (!expected %in% c(13L, 15L)) {
    warning(sprintf("%s: unexpected field count %d", path, expected))
  }
  cols_to_use <- if (expected == 15L) BED_COLS_15 else BED_COLS_13

  # A rare fiberHMM writer bug fuses blockEl/blockEr with no delimiter. Drop
  # those rows rather than failing the whole import.
  # FIX B1: dropping rows here used to silently break compute_msp_motif_stats(),
  #         which recovered `chrom` by matching row POSITION against a separate
  #         readLines() of the same file. `chrom` is now carried through here,
  #         so a dropped row can no longer shift the chromosome assignment.
  bad <- which(n_fields != expected)
  if (length(bad) > 0) {
    warning(sprintf("%s: %d malformed row(s) dropped (lines: %s%s)",
                    path, length(bad), paste(head(bad, 10), collapse = ", "),
                    if (length(bad) > 10) ", ..." else ""))
    lines <- lines[-bad]
  }

  raw <- read_tsv(
    I(paste(lines, collapse = "\n")),
    col_names = cols_to_use,
    col_types = cols(.default    = col_character(),
                     chromStart  = "i", chromEnd   = "i",
                     score       = "i", thickStart = "i",
                     thickEnd    = "i", blockCount = "i")
  )

  reads_tbl <- raw %>%
    transmute(
      chrom,
      read_name  = name,
      read_start = chromStart + 1L,   # 0-based -> 1-based inclusive
      read_end   = chromEnd,
      read_score = score,
      strand
    )

  has_tq <- "blockTq" %in% names(raw)

  # FIX B3: blockTq used to be unnested unconditionally. For 13-column files it
  #         was created as vector("list", n) -- a length-0 entry per row --
  #         and unnesting that against length-k blockSizes is version-dependent
  #         at best. No-op for 15-column files; makes the 13-column path safe.
  fp_base <- raw %>%
    transmute(
      chrom,
      read_name   = name,                                    # BED col 4
      .read0      = chromStart,                              # 0-based read start
      blockSizes  = lapply(strsplit(blockSizes,  ","), as.integer),
      chromStarts = lapply(strsplit(chromStarts, ","), as.integer),
      blockTq     = if (has_tq) lapply(strsplit(blockTq, ","), as.integer) else NULL
    )

  unnest_cols <- if (has_tq) c("blockSizes", "chromStarts", "blockTq")
                 else        c("blockSizes", "chromStarts")

  fps_tbl <- fp_base %>%
    unnest(all_of(unnest_cols)) %>%
    mutate(
      fp_start = .read0 + chromStarts + 1L,                  # 1-based inclusive
      fp_end   = .read0 + chromStarts + blockSizes,
      fp_width = blockSizes
    ) %>%
    select(chrom, read_name, fp_start, fp_end, fp_width, any_of("blockTq"))

  list(reads = reads_tbl, footprints = fps_tbl)
}
```

## 5.2 Building per-sample bundles

```{r fn-bundles}
#' Reads overlapping cluster_range, plus ALL of those reads' footprints
#'
#' Footprints are deliberately NOT clipped here: the clustering matrix clips to
#' cluster_range, the plot clips to plot_range, and those are different windows.
build_sample_bundle <- function(path, sample_name, cluster_range) {

  obj          <- read_fiberhmm_bed(path)
  region_chrom <- as.character(seqnames(cluster_range))
  region_start <- start(cluster_range)
  region_end   <- end(cluster_range)

  reads <- obj$reads %>%
    dplyr::filter(chrom == region_chrom,
                  read_end >= region_start, read_start <= region_end) %>%
    mutate(unique_id = paste0(sample_name, "_", read_name))

  if (nrow(reads) == 0) return(NULL)

  footprints <- obj$footprints %>%
    dplyr::filter(read_name %in% reads$read_name) %>%
    mutate(unique_id = paste0(sample_name, "_", read_name))

  list(reads = reads, footprints = footprints,
       region_start = region_start, region_end = region_end)
}

#' Run build_sample_bundle() over a named vector of paths
build_all_bundles <- function(files, cluster_range) {

  missing <- files[!file.exists(files)]
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    stop("File(s) not found:\n", paste(missing, collapse = "\n"))
  }

  bundles <- imap(files, ~ build_sample_bundle(.x, .y, cluster_range))

  empty <- names(Filter(is.null, bundles))
  if (length(empty) > 0) {
    message("Samples with 0 reads in cluster_range (dropped): ",
            paste(empty, collapse = ", "))
  }

  bundles <- compact(bundles)
  if (length(bundles) == 0) stop("No reads overlapped cluster_range in any sample.")
  bundles
}
```

## 5.3 Merging replicates for joint clustering

<!-- ==========================================================================
     Replicates are clustered TOGETHER so that a cluster means the same thing
     in rep1 and rep2, then split back apart for the per-replicate log2FC.

     Each read is re-stamped
         unique_id = "<merged_name>_<orig_sample>READSEP<orig_read_name>"
     cluster_reads() parses the merged name off the front and
     split_cluster_assignments() reverses the READSEP token.
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r fn-merge-split}
READSEP <- "READSEP"

merge_replicate_bundles <- function(bundles, merge_groups) {

  missing_samples <- base::setdiff(unlist(merge_groups), names(bundles))
  if (length(missing_samples) > 0) {
    stop("merge_replicate_bundles: sample(s) not in bundles: ",
         paste(missing_samples, collapse = ", "))
  }

  imap(merge_groups, function(orig_samples, merged_name) {

    parts <- bundles[orig_samples]

    restamp <- function(df, s_name) {
      df %>% mutate(
        orig_read_name = sub(paste0("^", s_name, "_"), "", unique_id),
        unique_id      = paste0(merged_name, "_", s_name, READSEP, orig_read_name)
      )
    }

    list(
      reads        = imap_dfr(parts, function(b, s) restamp(b$reads,      s)),
      footprints   = imap_dfr(parts, function(b, s) restamp(b$footprints, s)),
      region_start = parts[[1]]$region_start,
      region_end   = parts[[1]]$region_end
    )
  })
}

#' Expand merged cluster assignments back to one row per (replicate, read)
split_cluster_assignments <- function(cluster_assignments_merged) {

  merged_rows <- grepl(READSEP, cluster_assignments_merged$read_id, fixed = TRUE)

  if (!any(merged_rows)) {
    warning("split_cluster_assignments: no '", READSEP, "' token found. ",
            "Were these produced by merge_replicate_bundles()? Returning input.")
    return(cluster_assignments_merged)
  }

  cluster_assignments_merged %>%
    dplyr::filter(merged_rows) %>%
    mutate(
      orig_sample    = sub(paste0(READSEP, ".*$"), "", read_id),
      orig_read_name = sub(paste0("^.*", READSEP), "", read_id)
    ) %>%
    transmute(
      unique_id = paste0(orig_sample, "_", orig_read_name),
      cluster,
      Sample    = orig_sample,
      read_id   = orig_read_name
    )
}
```

## 5.4 Occupancy matrix and k-means clustering

```{r fn-cluster}
#' Binary nucleosome-occupancy matrix: rows = reads, columns = bp of cluster_range
bundle_to_matrix <- function(bundle) {

  region_start <- bundle$region_start
  region_end   <- bundle$region_end
  width_range  <- region_end - region_start + 1L

  reads <- bundle$reads
  mat   <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(reads), ncol = width_range,
                  dimnames = list(reads$unique_id, NULL))

  ft <- bundle$footprints %>%
    dplyr::filter(fp_end >= region_start, fp_start <= region_end) %>%
    mutate(rel_start = pmax(1L,           fp_start - region_start + 1L),
           rel_end   = pmin(width_range,  fp_end   - region_start + 1L))

  row_idx <- match(ft$unique_id, rownames(mat))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(ft))) {
    if (!is.na(row_idx[i])) mat[row_idx[i], ft$rel_start[i]:ft$rel_end[i]] <- 1
  }
  mat
}

#' k-means that does not depend on the order rows were stacked in
#'
#' PROBLEM : kmeans(centers = <a number>) chooses its initial
#' centres by SAMPLING ROWS of the matrix. Two runs with the same seed but a
#' different row order therefore start from different centres and can land in
#' different local optima. In this dataset that was worth ~11% of reads.
#'
#' FIX, in two parts:
#'   1. the caller sorts rows into a canonical order before calling this;
#'   2. the random restarts are run on a SUBSAMPLE to find good centres, then a
#'      single pass over the full matrix refines them. Passing `centers` as a
#'      matrix makes that final pass fully deterministic -- no sampling at all.
#'
#' Why subsample: nstart = 200 on ~180k x ~400 is hours of compute, and nstart
#' = 25 was demonstrably too few to converge on a stable partition. Running 200
#' starts on 20k rows explores far more of the space for a fraction of the cost,
#' and the full-data refinement recovers the exact centres.
#'
#' @return the kmeans object, plus $init_method describing how it was seeded
kmeans_stable <- function(mat, k,
                          seed      = KMEANS_SEED,
                          nstart    = KMEANS_NSTART,
                          iter_max  = KMEANS_ITER_MAX,
                          subsample = KMEANS_SUBSAMPLE) {

  set.seed(seed)

  if (is.null(subsample) || nrow(mat) <= subsample) {
    km <- kmeans(mat, centers = k, nstart = nstart, iter.max = iter_max)
    km$init_method <- sprintf("full data, nstart = %d", nstart)
  } else {
    idx <- sort(sample.int(nrow(mat), subsample))
    km0 <- kmeans(mat[idx, , drop = FALSE], centers = k,
                  nstart = nstart, iter.max = iter_max)
    # a degenerate subsample can yield an empty centre; refuse rather than
    # silently return fewer than k clusters
    if (nrow(km0$centers) < k) {
      stop("kmeans_stable: subsample produced only ", nrow(km0$centers),
           " of ", k, " centres. Increase KMEANS_SUBSAMPLE or lower k.")
    }
    km <- kmeans(mat, centers = km0$centers, iter.max = iter_max)
    km$init_method <- sprintf("centres from %d-row subsample, nstart = %d, then one full pass",
                              subsample, nstart)
  }

  if (!is.null(km$ifault) && km$ifault == 4L) {
    warning("kmeans did not converge in ", iter_max,
            " iterations -- raise KMEANS_ITER_MAX.")
  }
  km
}

#' Pool every sample's reads, k-means, then relabel clusters by "openness"
#'
#' After k-means the clusters are RENUMBERED by mean nucleosome occupancy,
#' ascending: cluster 1 = fewest nucleosomes = most open, cluster k = most
#' nucleosome-occupied. Set rank_clusters = FALSE to keep k-means' arbitrary
#' labels.
#'
#' @return tibble(unique_id, Sample, read_id, cluster) with attr "kmeans_info"
cluster_reads <- function(bundles, k, seed = KMEANS_SEED, rank_clusters = TRUE,
                          nstart = KMEANS_NSTART, subsample = KMEANS_SUBSAMPLE) {

  master_mat <- do.call(rbind, map(bundles, bundle_to_matrix))

  # FIX C7, part 1: canonical row order, so the clustering depends only on the
  # reads / k / seed and not on how the bundles happened to be stacked.
  # method = "radix" sorts in C collation, which is locale-independent --
  # plain order() on strings can differ between machines and locales.
  master_mat <- master_mat[order(rownames(master_mat), method = "radix"), ,
                           drop = FALSE]

  if (anyDuplicated(rownames(master_mat))) {
    stop("cluster_reads: duplicated read ids in the pooled matrix. ",
         "Two bundles are contributing the same unique_id.")
  }

  km         <- kmeans_stable(master_mat, k = k, seed = seed,
                              nstart = nstart, subsample = subsample)
  cluster_id <- km$cluster

  if (rank_clusters) {
    clust_signal <- tapply(rowMeans(master_mat), cluster_id, mean)
    relabel      <- setNames(rank(clust_signal, ties.method = "first"),
                             names(clust_signal))
    cluster_id   <- as.integer(relabel[as.character(cluster_id)])
  }

  sample_names <- names(bundles)
  ordered      <- sample_names[order(nchar(sample_names), decreasing = TRUE)]
  prefixes     <- paste0(ordered, "_")

  ids <- rownames(master_mat)
  hit <- rep(NA_integer_, length(ids))
  for (i in seq_along(prefixes)) {
    todo      <- is.na(hit) & startsWith(ids, prefixes[i])
    hit[todo] <- i
  }

  if (anyNA(hit)) {
    stop("cluster_reads: ", sum(is.na(hit)), " read id(s) matched no sample name. ",
         "First offender: ", ids[which(is.na(hit))[1]])
  }

  smp <- ordered[hit]

  out <- tibble(
    unique_id = ids,
    Sample    = smp,
    read_id   = substring(ids, nchar(smp) + 2L),   # drop "<Sample>_"
    cluster   = factor(cluster_id, levels = seq_len(k))
  )

  # Record how well this fit actually did, so two runs can be compared on
  # something better than eyeballing the panels. tot_withinss is the quantity
  # k-means minimises: lower is a better fit to the SAME data at the SAME k.
  attr(out, "kmeans_info") <- list(
    k             = k,
    seed          = seed,
    nstart        = nstart,
    subsample     = subsample,
    init_method   = km$init_method,
    n_reads       = nrow(master_mat),
    n_positions   = ncol(master_mat),
    tot_withinss  = km$tot.withinss,
    betweenss     = km$betweenss,
    prop_between  = km$betweenss / km$totss,
    iterations    = km$iter,
    cluster_sizes = as.integer(table(factor(cluster_id, levels = seq_len(k))))
  )
  out
}

#' Agreement between two clusterings of the same reads (Adjusted Rand Index)
#'
#' 1 = identical up to relabelling, ~0 = no better than chance. Use it to check
#' whether a partition is a property of the data or of the random seed.
adjusted_rand <- function(a, b) {
  tab <- table(a, b)
  nij <- sum(choose(tab, 2))
  ai  <- sum(choose(rowSums(tab), 2))
  bj  <- sum(choose(colSums(tab), 2))
  n   <- choose(sum(tab), 2)
  exp <- ai * bj / n
  (nij - exp) / ((ai + bj) / 2 - exp)
}

#' One row per footprint, tagged with its cluster, restricted to plot_range,
#' with a within-(Sample, cluster) stacking index for drawing.
prepare_plot_data <- function(bundles, cluster_assignments, plot_range) {

  imap_dfr(bundles, function(b, s_name) {
    b$footprints %>%
      transmute(unique_id, Sample = s_name,
                start = fp_start, end = fp_end, width = fp_width)
  }) %>%
    inner_join(cluster_assignments, by = c("unique_id", "Sample")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(start <= end(plot_range), end >= start(plot_range)) %>%
    arrange(Sample, cluster, unique_id) %>%
    group_by(Sample, cluster) %>%
    mutate(local_index = as.numeric(factor(unique_id, levels = unique(unique_id)))) %>%
    ungroup()
}
```

## 5.5 Shared coverage helpers

```{r fn-coverage}
#' Look up a per-sample fill colour: exact name, then regex, then a warned default
.resolve_fill <- function(s, fill_color, default = "grey30") {
  if (is.null(names(fill_color))) return(fill_color[[1]])
  if (s %in% names(fill_color))   return(unname(fill_color[[s]]))
  hit <- names(fill_color)[vapply(names(fill_color),
                                  function(p) grepl(p, s), logical(1))]
  if (length(hit) >= 1) return(unname(fill_color[[hit[1]]]))
  warning(sprintf("No fill colour matched sample '%s'; using %s", s, default))
  default
}

#' Per-bp integer coverage over [region_start, region_end] from a set of intervals
#'
#' FIX B2: intervals lying entirely OUTSIDE the region give s > e after
#'         clipping. `s:e` then counts downwards and adds coverage at the wrong
#'         positions instead of adding none. This matters because reads are
#'         selected on cluster_range but coverage is computed on plot_range,
#'         so a read outside plot_range is perfectly possible. Now dropped.
.coverage_vector <- function(starts, ends, region_start, region_end) {

  n_pos   <- region_end - region_start + 1L
  cov_vec <- integer(n_pos)
  if (length(starts) == 0) return(cov_vec)

  s <- pmax(starts, region_start) - region_start + 1L
  e <- pmin(ends,   region_end)   - region_start + 1L

  keep <- which(e >= s)                    # <-- the guard
  for (i in keep) cov_vec[s[i]:e[i]] <- cov_vec[s[i]:e[i]] + 1L
  cov_vec
}

#' Every read's extent + Sample, tagged with its cluster.
#' This is the per-bp read-coverage DENOMINATOR for every metaplot below.
reads_with_clusters <- function(bundles, cluster_assignments) {
  imap_dfr(bundles, function(b, s_name) {
    b$reads %>% transmute(Sample = s_name, unique_id, read_start, read_end)
  }) %>%
    inner_join(cluster_assignments %>% select(Sample, unique_id, cluster),
               by = c("Sample", "unique_id"))
}
```

## 5.6 Per-cluster log2 fold change

<!-- ==========================================================================
     `comparisons` is a named list; each element is a length-2 NAMED vector
         c(numerator = "<sample>", denominator = "<sample>")
     compute_log2fc_df() computes, per cluster, the % of that sample's reads
     falling in the cluster, then log2(numerator% / denominator%).
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r fn-log2fc}
#' @param min_reads     read-count floor for the "low coverage" flag
#' @param low_cov_rule  "both"   flag only if BOTH sides are below min_reads
#'                               (original behaviour -- see reviewer note Q2)
#'                      "either" flag if EITHER side is below min_reads
#'                               (the more conservative rule)
compute_log2fc_df <- function(cluster_assignments, comparisons,
                              min_reads    = MIN_READS_FC,
                              low_cov_rule = LOW_COV_RULE) {

  low_cov_rule <- match.arg(low_cov_rule, c("both", "either"))

  cluster_stats <- cluster_assignments %>%
    dplyr::count(Sample, cluster, name = "n_reads") %>%
    group_by(Sample) %>%
    mutate(percent = 100 * n_reads / sum(n_reads)) %>%
    ungroup()

  percent_wide <- cluster_stats %>%
    select(Sample, cluster, percent) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Sample, values_from = percent, values_fill = 0)

  reads_wide <- cluster_stats %>%
    select(Sample, cluster, n_reads) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Sample, values_from = n_reads, values_fill = 0)

  imap_dfr(comparisons, function(pair, label) {

    num <- pair[["numerator"]]
    den <- pair[["denominator"]]

    missing <- base::setdiff(c(num, den), names(percent_wide))
    if (length(missing) > 0) {
      stop("Comparison '", label, "' references sample(s) not in ",
           "cluster_assignments: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
    }

    # a sample absent from reads_wide has 0 reads in every cluster
    num_reads <- if (num %in% names(reads_wide)) reads_wide[[num]] else rep(0L, nrow(reads_wide))
    den_reads <- if (den %in% names(reads_wide)) reads_wide[[den]] else rep(0L, nrow(reads_wide))

    low <- if (low_cov_rule == "both") {
      num_reads < min_reads & den_reads < min_reads
    } else {
      num_reads < min_reads | den_reads < min_reads
    }

    pct_num <- percent_wide[[num]]
    pct_den <- percent_wide[[den]]

    tibble(
      cluster        = percent_wide$cluster,
      Replicate_Pair = label,
      num_reads      = num_reads,
      den_reads      = den_reads,
      Log2Ratio      = log2(pct_num / pct_den),
      # A cluster emptied (or created) by the treatment gives +/-Inf. That is a
      # real result, not a defect -- but geom_col silently DROPS non-finite
      # values, so without this flag the strongest effect on the panel would be
      # the one bar you could not see. make_log2fc_panel() draws these clamped
      # to the panel edge with a marker.
      status = dplyr::case_when(
        num_reads == 0 & den_reads == 0 ~ "no reads",
        num_reads == 0                  ~ "complete loss",
        den_reads == 0                  ~ "complete gain",
        TRUE                            ~ "ok"
      )
    ) %>%
      left_join(tibble(cluster = reads_wide$cluster, low_coverage = low),
                by = "cluster")
  })
}

#' Horizontal log2FC bar panel, one facet row per cluster.
#' Designed to sit alongside a heatmap that uses the same
#' facet_grid(space = "free_y") cluster rows.
make_log2fc_panel <- function(log2fc_df, title = "Fold change",
                              palette = twist_palette,
                              xlim = NULL,
                              low_coverage_color = "grey70",
                              low_coverage_label = "low coverage",
                              show_boundary = TRUE) {

  if (!"low_coverage" %in% names(log2fc_df)) log2fc_df$low_coverage <- FALSE
  if (!"status" %in% names(log2fc_df))       log2fc_df$status <- "ok"

  # A cluster that the treatment empties gives log2 = -Inf (or +Inf if it
  # appears only after treatment). geom_col drops non-finite values without
  # comment, so the strongest effect on the panel would otherwise be invisible.
  # Clamp those bars to the panel edge and mark them, leaving every finite
  # value exactly as computed -- no pseudocount, nothing rescaled.
  finite_vals <- log2fc_df$Log2Ratio[is.finite(log2fc_df$Log2Ratio)]
  edge <- if (!is.null(xlim)) {
    max(abs(xlim))
  } else if (length(finite_vals) > 0) {
    max(abs(finite_vals)) * 1.15
  } else 1

  log2fc_df <- log2fc_df %>%
    mutate(
      is_boundary = !is.finite(Log2Ratio) & !is.na(Log2Ratio),
      Log2Plot    = ifelse(is_boundary, sign(Log2Ratio) * edge, Log2Ratio),
      # collapse the fill grouping so every flagged bar shares one grey category
      fill_group  = ifelse(low_coverage, low_coverage_label,
                           as.character(Replicate_Pair))
    )

  rp_levels   <- unique(as.character(log2fc_df$Replicate_Pair))
  fill_values <- setNames(palette[seq_along(rp_levels)], rp_levels)
  fill_values[low_coverage_label] <- low_coverage_color

  p <- ggplot(log2fc_df, aes(x = Log2Plot, y = Replicate_Pair, fill = fill_group)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
    facet_grid(cluster ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_values) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 3)) +
    labs(x = "Log2(ratio)", y = NULL, fill = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      axis.text.y       = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y      = element_blank(),
      axis.line         = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing     = unit(0, "lines"),
      panel.border      = element_blank(),
      strip.background  = element_blank(),
      strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = 7, face = "bold",
                                       margin = margin(r = 4, l = 2)),
      legend.position   = "bottom",
      plot.title        = element_text(size = 10)
    ) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -Inf, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3)

  # arrowhead at the clamped end, so the bar reads as "runs off the scale"
  # rather than as a real value at the panel limit
  if (show_boundary && any(log2fc_df$is_boundary)) {
    bd <- log2fc_df %>% dplyr::filter(is_boundary)
    p <- p +
      geom_segment(data = bd,
                   aes(x = Log2Plot * 0.75, xend = Log2Plot,
                       y = Replicate_Pair, yend = Replicate_Pair),
                   inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3,
                   arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.05, "in"), type = "closed")) +
      geom_text(data = bd,
                aes(x = Log2Plot * 0.5, y = Replicate_Pair,
                    label = ifelse(Log2Ratio < 0, "0 reads after", "0 reads before")),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black",
                size = 2.2, fontface = "italic", vjust = -1)
  }

  if (any(log2fc_df$low_coverage)) {
    lbl_df <- log2fc_df %>%
      dplyr::filter(low_coverage) %>%
      distinct(cluster, Replicate_Pair) %>%
      mutate(x = 0)
    p <- p + geom_text(data = lbl_df,
                       aes(x = x, y = Replicate_Pair, label = low_coverage_label),
                       inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black",
                       size = 2.5, fontface = "italic")
  }

  if (!is.null(xlim)) p <- p + coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim)
  p
}
```

## 5.7 Dense per-sample heatmap (independent panels)

```{r fn-dense}
#' One patchwork panel per sample, faceted by cluster.
#' Pass log2fc_df to append a fold-change bar panel on the right.
plot_fiberseq_dense <- function(plot_df, plot_range, sample_order,
                                vlines = NULL, vline_colors = NULL,
                                fill_color = TF_FILL,
                                binding_sites = NULL,
                                title = "Clustered Fiber-seq: dense per-cell view",
                                log2fc_df = NULL,
                                log2fc_title = "Fold change",
                                log2fc_palette = twist_palette,
                                log2fc_width = 0.5,
                                log2fc_xlim = NULL,
                                raster = TRUE, raster_dpi = 300,
                                xlab = NULL) {

  chr  <- as.character(seqnames(plot_range))
  xlab <- xlab %||% paste0("Genomic coordinate (", chr, ")")

  plot_df <- plot_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(Sample %in% sample_order) %>%
    mutate(Sample = factor(Sample, levels = sample_order))

  plot_xlim <- c(start(plot_range), end(plot_range))
  if (!is.null(vlines) && is.null(vline_colors)) {
    vline_colors <- rep("black", length(vlines))
  }

  make_sample_panel <- function(s) {

    df_s  <- plot_df %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == s)
    col_s <- .resolve_fill(s, fill_color)

    rect_layer <- geom_rect(
      data = df_s,
      aes(xmin = pmax(start, plot_xlim[1]),
          xmax = pmin(end,   plot_xlim[2]),
          ymin = local_index - 0.45,
          ymax = local_index + 0.45),
      fill = col_s, colour = NA
    )
    if (raster) {
      rect_layer <- ggrastr::rasterise(rect_layer, dpi = raster_dpi, dev = "ragg_png")
    }

    sample_label <- data.frame(
      x = mean(plot_xlim), y = Inf, label = s,
      cluster = factor(levels(df_s$cluster)[1], levels = levels(df_s$cluster))
    )

    p <- ggplot(df_s) +
      rect_layer +
      facet_grid(cluster ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = plot_xlim, clip = "off") +
      theme_classic() +
      theme(
        axis.text.y       = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y      = element_blank(),
        axis.line         = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing     = unit(0, "lines"),
        strip.background  = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = 7,
                                         margin = margin(r = 4, l = 2)),
        panel.border      = element_blank(),
        plot.margin       = margin(t = 40, r = 5, b = 5, l = 5)
      ) +
      labs(title = NULL, y = NULL, x = xlab) +
      geom_text(data = sample_label, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
                vjust = -3, size = 3.5, inherit.aes = FALSE)

    if (!is.null(binding_sites)) {
      bs_labels <- binding_sites %>%
        mutate(cluster = factor(levels(df_s$cluster)[1],
                                levels = levels(df_s$cluster)))
      p <- p +
        geom_rect(data = binding_sites,
                  aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = col),
                  alpha = 1, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
        scale_fill_identity(guide = "none") +
        geom_text(data = bs_labels,
                  aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = Inf, label = TF, colour = col),
                  vjust = -1, size = 3, fontface = "bold",
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE) +
        scale_colour_identity(guide = "none")
    }
    p
  }

  plots <- lapply(sample_order, make_sample_panel)
  n_s   <- length(sample_order)

  if (!is.null(log2fc_df)) {
    bar_panel <- make_log2fc_panel(log2fc_df, title = log2fc_title,
                                   palette = log2fc_palette, xlim = log2fc_xlim)
    wrap_plots(c(plots, list(bar_panel)), nrow = 1) +
      plot_layout(widths = c(rep(1, n_s), log2fc_width)) +
      plot_annotation(title = title)
  } else {
    wrap_plots(plots, nrow = 1) + plot_annotation(title = title)
  }
}
```

## 5.8 Metaplots

<!-- ==========================================================================
     OCCUPANCY, both flavours:
         occupancy(bp) = footprints_covering(bp) / read_coverage(bp) * 100
     with bp below min_read_cov spanning reads set to NA.

     They differ ONLY in the read-coverage DENOMINATOR:
       NUCLEOSOME metaplots : normalised over WHOLE-SAMPLE depth, i.e. all of
                              that sample's reads at each bp across every
                              cluster, so per-cluster curves share one scale.
       TF metaplots         : normalised PER CLUSTER, i.e. only reads in the
                              cluster being drawn.
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r fn-nuc-metaplot}
#' Per-cluster nucleosome occupancy, normalised over whole-sample depth
compute_cluster_metaplot <- function(plot_df, cluster_assignments, plot_range,
                                     bundles, clusters = NULL,
                                     min_read_cov = MIN_READ_COV) {

  region_start <- start(plot_range)
  region_end   <- end(plot_range)
  pos_vec      <- region_start:region_end

  # denominator: per-bp read coverage from ALL reads of each sample
  reads_df        <- reads_with_clusters(bundles, cluster_assignments)
  samples_present <- unique(reads_df$Sample)

  read_cov_by_sample <- setNames(lapply(samples_present, function(s_name) {
    r <- reads_df[reads_df$Sample == s_name, ]
    .coverage_vector(r$read_start, r$read_end, region_start, region_end)
  }), samples_present)

  df <- plot_df
  if (!is.null(clusters)) {
    df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(as.character(cluster) %in% as.character(clusters))
  }

  groups <- df %>% distinct(Sample, cluster)

  purrr::map2_dfr(groups$Sample, groups$cluster, function(s_name, c_name) {
    # base-R subsetting to avoid NSE name collisions with the column names
    sub      <- df[df$Sample == s_name & df$cluster == c_name, ]
    fp_cov   <- .coverage_vector(sub$start, sub$end, region_start, region_end)
    read_cov <- read_cov_by_sample[[s_name]]

    tibble(Sample = s_name, cluster = c_name, pos = pos_vec,
           fp_coverage   = fp_cov,
           read_coverage = read_cov,
           normalized_occupancy = ifelse(read_cov >= min_read_cov,
                                         fp_cov / read_cov * 100, NA_real_))
  })
}

#' Draw a per-bp occupancy table: one panel per cluster, samples overlaid
plot_cluster_metaplot <- function(metaplot_df, plot_range,
                                  clusters = NULL, samples = NULL,
                                  free_y = FALSE,
                                  binding_sites = NULL,
                                  vlines = NULL, vline_colors = NULL,
                                  sample_colors = NULL,
                                  title = "Nucleosome footprint metaplot by cluster",
                                  subtitle = "Occupancy = footprints / read coverage x 100") {

  metaplot_df <- metaplot_df %>% mutate(cluster = as.character(cluster))

  if (!is.null(samples)) {
    metaplot_df <- metaplot_df %>%
      dplyr::filter(Sample %in% samples) %>%
      mutate(Sample = factor(Sample, levels = samples))
  }

  if (!is.null(clusters)) {
    clusters    <- as.character(clusters)
    metaplot_df <- metaplot_df %>%
      dplyr::filter(cluster %in% clusters) %>%
      mutate(cluster = factor(cluster, levels = clusters))
  } else {
    lvls        <- as.character(sort(as.integer(unique(metaplot_df$cluster))))
    metaplot_df <- metaplot_df %>% mutate(cluster = factor(cluster, levels = lvls))
  }

  if (!is.null(vlines) && is.null(vline_colors)) {
    vline_colors <- rep("black", length(vlines))
  }

  p <- ggplot(metaplot_df, aes(x = pos, y = normalized_occupancy))

  # motif bands first, on their own identity scales, then hand the fill/colour
  # scales back to the Sample aesthetics via ggnewscale
  if (!is.null(binding_sites)) {
    p <- p +
      geom_rect(data = binding_sites,
                aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = col),
                alpha = 0.15, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      scale_fill_identity(guide = "none") +
      geom_text(data = binding_sites,
                aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = Inf, label = TF, colour = col),
                vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
                inherit.aes = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE) +
      scale_colour_identity(guide = "none") +
      ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
      ggnewscale::new_scale_colour()
  }

  p <- p +
    geom_area(aes(fill = Sample), position = "identity", alpha = 0.1) +
    geom_line(aes(colour = Sample), linewidth = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~ cluster, scales = if (free_y) "free_y" else "fixed",
               ncol = 1, strip.position = "right") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(start(plot_range), end(plot_range))) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
         x = "Genomic coordinate", y = "Occupancy %") +
    theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"),
          panel.spacing    = unit(0.2, "lines"))

  p <- p + if (!is.null(sample_colors)) {
    list(scale_colour_manual(values = sample_colors),
         scale_fill_manual(values   = sample_colors))
  } else {
    list(scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1"),
         scale_fill_brewer(palette   = "Set1"))
  }

  if (!is.null(vlines)) {
    for (i in seq_along(vlines)) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = vlines[i], linetype = "dashed",
                          linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5, colour = vline_colors[i])
    }
  }
  p
}
```

```{r fn-tf-metaplot}
#' Load TF footprint files and inherit each footprint's cluster from its
#' parent read's NUCLEOSOME cluster.
#'
#' A TF footprint is kept only if (a) its blockTq quality passes
#' score_threshold, (b) it is no wider than max_width, (c) it overlaps
#' plot_range, and (d) its read was assigned a cluster upstream.
build_tf_metaplot_data <- function(tf_files, cluster_assignments, plot_range,
                                   score_threshold = TF_SCORE_THR,
                                   max_width = TF_MAX_WIDTH) {

  missing <- tf_files[!file.exists(tf_files)]
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    stop("TF file(s) not found:\n", paste(missing, collapse = "\n"))
  }

  region_chrom <- as.character(seqnames(plot_range))
  region_start <- start(plot_range)
  region_end   <- end(plot_range)

  clust_lookup <- cluster_assignments %>% select(Sample, unique_id, cluster)

  tf_df <- imap_dfr(tf_files, function(path, s_name) {

    raw_fps <- read_fiberhmm_bed(path)$footprints

    # blockTq is fiberHMM's tf.QQQ quality byte. blockEl / blockEr are
    # edge-sharpness bytes and must NOT be used as a quality score.
    fps <- raw_fps %>%
      transmute(
        Sample    = s_name,
        unique_id = paste0(s_name, "_", read_name),
        chrom,
        start     = fp_start,
        end       = fp_end,
        width     = fp_width,
        score     = if ("blockTq" %in% names(raw_fps)) raw_fps$blockTq
                    else rep(NA_integer_, nrow(raw_fps))
      )

    if (!is.null(score_threshold)) {
      if (all(is.na(fps$score))) {
        warning(sprintf("%s: score_threshold ignored -- no blockTq column", s_name))
      } else {
        fps <- fps %>% dplyr::filter(score >= score_threshold)
      }
    }
    if (!is.null(max_width)) fps <- fps %>% dplyr::filter(width <= max_width)

    fps %>% dplyr::filter(chrom == region_chrom,
                          start <= region_end, end >= region_start)
  })

  tf_df %>% inner_join(clust_lookup, by = c("Sample", "unique_id"))
}

#' Per-bp TF occupancy.
#' pool_clusters = FALSE : one curve per (sample, cluster), denominator = that
#'                         cluster's reads
#' pool_clusters = TRUE  : one curve per sample, denominator = all reads (or
#'                         all reads in `clusters`, if given)
compute_tf_metaplot <- function(tf_df, cluster_assignments, plot_range,
                                bundles, clusters = NULL, pool_clusters = FALSE,
                                min_read_cov = MIN_READ_COV) {

  region_start <- start(plot_range)
  region_end   <- end(plot_range)
  pos_vec      <- region_start:region_end

  reads_df <- reads_with_clusters(bundles, cluster_assignments)
  df       <- tf_df

  if (!is.null(clusters)) {
    df       <- df       %>% dplyr::filter(as.character(cluster) %in% as.character(clusters))
    reads_df <- reads_df %>% dplyr::filter(as.character(cluster) %in% as.character(clusters))
  }

  fp_cov <- function(sub) .coverage_vector(sub$start,      sub$end,      region_start, region_end)
  rd_cov <- function(sub) .coverage_vector(sub$read_start, sub$read_end, region_start, region_end)
  to_occ <- function(fp, rd) ifelse(rd >= min_read_cov, fp / rd * 100, NA_real_)

  if (pool_clusters) {
    purrr::map_dfr(unique(df$Sample), function(s_name) {
      fp <- fp_cov(df[df$Sample == s_name, ])
      rd <- rd_cov(reads_df[reads_df$Sample == s_name, ])
      tibble(Sample = s_name, pos = pos_vec,
             fp_coverage = fp, read_coverage = rd,
             normalized_occupancy = to_occ(fp, rd))
    })
  } else {
    groups <- df %>% distinct(Sample, cluster)
    purrr::map2_dfr(groups$Sample, groups$cluster, function(s_name, c_name) {
      fp <- fp_cov(df[df$Sample == s_name & df$cluster == c_name, ])
      rd <- rd_cov(reads_df[reads_df$Sample == s_name & reads_df$cluster == c_name, ])
      tibble(Sample = s_name, cluster = c_name, pos = pos_vec,
             fp_coverage = fp, read_coverage = rd,
             normalized_occupancy = to_occ(fp, rd))
    })
  }
}

#' Thin wrapper: per-cluster TF panel
plot_tf_metaplot <- function(tf_metaplot_df, plot_range, ...,
                             title = "TF footprint metaplot by cluster",

  plot_cluster_metaplot(tf_metaplot_df, plot_range, ...,
                        title = title, subtitle = subtitle)
}

#' Average replicates of a per-bp metaplot table into one curve per condition.
#'
#' Replaces merge_reps() / merge_snai_reps(), which were defined five times in
#' the old document with three different output label conventions (C5).
average_replicates <- function(df, keep_timepoint = FALSE) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      .tf   = ifelse(grepl("TWIST1", Sample), "TWIST1", "SNAI"),
      .trt  = ifelse(grepl("DMSO",   Sample), "DMSO",   "dTag"),
      .time = stringr::str_extract(Sample, "\\d+min"),
      condition = if (keep_timepoint) paste(.tf, .trt, .time, sep = "_")
                  else                paste(.tf, .trt, sep = "_")
    ) %>%
    group_by(condition, pos) %>%
    summarise(normalized_occupancy = mean(normalized_occupancy, na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::rename(Sample = condition)
}
```
