```{r fn-pooled-and-midpoint}
#' Pool a set of clusters into ONE occupancy curve per sample.
#' denominator = "cluster" : normalise over reads in those clusters only
#' denominator = "all"     : normalise over every read in the region
compute_pooled_cluster_metaplot <- function(plot_df, cluster_assignments, plot_range,
                                            bundles, clusters,
                                            min_read_cov = MIN_READ_COV,
                                            denominator = c("cluster", "all")) {

  denominator  <- match.arg(denominator)
  region_start <- start(plot_range)
  region_end   <- end(plot_range)
  pos_vec      <- region_start:region_end

  df <- plot_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(as.integer(as.character(cluster)) %in% as.integer(clusters))

  reads_df_all <- reads_with_clusters(bundles, cluster_assignments)
  reads_df     <- if (denominator == "cluster") {
    reads_df_all %>%
      dplyr::filter(as.integer(as.character(cluster)) %in% as.integer(clusters))
  } else reads_df_all

  purrr::map_dfr(unique(df$Sample), function(s_name) {
    fp <- .coverage_vector(df$start[df$Sample == s_name],
                           df$end[df$Sample == s_name],
                           region_start, region_end)
    rd <- .coverage_vector(reads_df$read_start[reads_df$Sample == s_name],
                           reads_df$read_end[reads_df$Sample == s_name],
                           region_start, region_end)
    tibble(Sample = s_name, pos = pos_vec,
           fp_coverage = fp, read_coverage = rd,
           normalized_occupancy = ifelse(rd >= min_read_cov, fp / rd * 100, NA_real_))
  })
}

#' Nucleosome MIDPOINT density per bin (positioning/phasing rather than
#' occupancy), smoothed with a rolling mean.
compute_midpoint_metaplot <- function(plot_df, cluster_assignments, plot_range,
                                      bundles, clusters = NULL,
                                      bin_width = 10L, smooth_k = 5L,
                                      min_read_cov = MIN_READ_COV) {

  region_start <- start(plot_range)
  region_end   <- end(plot_range)

  df <- plot_df
  if (!is.null(clusters)) {
    df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(as.integer(as.character(cluster)) %in% as.integer(clusters))
  }
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(midpoint = (start + end) / 2) %>%
    dplyr::filter(midpoint >= region_start, midpoint <= region_end)

  reads_df <- reads_with_clusters(bundles, cluster_assignments)
  if (!is.null(clusters)) {
    reads_df <- reads_df %>%
      dplyr::filter(as.integer(as.character(cluster)) %in% as.integer(clusters))
  }

  bins <- seq(region_start, region_end - bin_width, by = bin_width)

  purrr::map_dfr(unique(df$Sample), function(s_name) {

    r <- reads_df %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == s_name)

    bin_counts <- df %>%
      dplyr::filter(Sample == s_name) %>%
      mutate(bin = floor((midpoint - region_start) / bin_width) * bin_width + region_start) %>%
      dplyr::count(bin, name = "n_midpoints")

    # denominator: reads spanning each bin CENTRE
    bin_cov <- purrr::map_int(bins, function(b) {
      centre <- b + bin_width / 2
      sum(r$read_start <= centre & r$read_end >= centre)
    })

    tibble(bin = bins, read_coverage = bin_cov) %>%
      left_join(bin_counts, by = "bin") %>%
      mutate(
        n_midpoints          = tidyr::replace_na(n_midpoints, 0L),
        normalized_occupancy = ifelse(read_coverage >= min_read_cov,
                                      n_midpoints / read_coverage * 100, NA_real_)
      ) %>%
      arrange(bin) %>%
      mutate(normalized_occupancy = zoo::rollmean(normalized_occupancy,
                                                  k = smooth_k, fill = NA,
                                                  align = "center"),
             Sample = s_name)
  })
}
```

## 5.9 ATAC-seq signal tracks

```{r fn-atac}
#' Tidy per-bp bigWig signal restricted to plot_range, one row per (Sample, bp)
compute_atac_signal <- function(atac_files, plot_range) {

  missing <- atac_files[!file.exists(atac_files)]
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    stop("bigWig file(s) not found:\n", paste(missing, collapse = "\n"))
  }

  region_start <- start(plot_range)
  region_end   <- end(plot_range)
  pos_vec      <- region_start:region_end

  imap_dfr(atac_files, function(path, s_name) {
    gr  <- rtracklayer::import.bw(path, which = plot_range)
    sig <- numeric(length(pos_vec))          # gaps stay 0, correct for bigWig
    if (length(gr) > 0) {
      s <- pmax(start(gr), region_start) - region_start + 1L
      e <- pmin(end(gr),   region_end)   - region_start + 1L
      for (i in which(e >= s)) sig[s[i]:e[i]] <- mcols(gr)$score[i]
    }
    tibble(Sample = s_name, pos = pos_vec, signal = sig)
  })
}

#' Standalone ATAC track, same visual conventions as the metaplots
plot_atac_signal <- function(atac_df, plot_range,
                             samples = NULL, facet = FALSE,
                             binding_sites = NULL,
                             vlines = NULL, vline_colors = NULL,
                             sample_colors = NULL,
                             title = "ATAC-seq signal", subtitle = NULL,
                             xlab = NULL) {

  region_start <- start(plot_range)
  region_end   <- end(plot_range)
  chr          <- as.character(seqnames(plot_range))
  xlab         <- xlab %||% paste0("Genomic coordinate (", chr, ")")

  df <- atac_df %>% dplyr::filter(pos >= region_start, pos <= region_end)
  if (!is.null(samples)) {
    df <- df %>%
      dplyr::filter(Sample %in% samples) %>%
      mutate(Sample = factor(Sample, levels = samples))
  }
  if (!is.null(vlines) && is.null(vline_colors)) {
    vline_colors <- rep("black", length(vlines))
  }

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = pos, y = signal))

  if (!is.null(binding_sites)) {
    p <- p +
      geom_rect(data = binding_sites,
                aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = col),
                alpha = 0.15, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      scale_fill_identity(guide = "none") +
      geom_text(data = binding_sites,
                aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = Inf, label = TF, colour = col),
                vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
                inherit.aes = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE) +
      scale_colour_identity(guide = "none") +
      ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
      ggnewscale::new_scale_colour()
  }

  p <- p +
    geom_area(aes(fill = Sample), position = "identity", alpha = 0.1) +
    geom_line(aes(colour = Sample), linewidth = 0.8) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(region_start, region_end)) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = xlab, y = "ATAC signal") +
    theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"))

  if (facet) p <- p + facet_wrap(~ Sample, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y",
                                 strip.position = "right")

  p <- p + if (!is.null(sample_colors)) {
    list(scale_colour_manual(values = sample_colors),
         scale_fill_manual(values   = sample_colors))
  } else {
    list(scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1"),
         scale_fill_brewer(palette   = "Set1"))
  }

  if (!is.null(vlines)) {
    for (i in seq_along(vlines)) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = vlines[i], linetype = "dashed",
                          linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5, colour = vline_colors[i])
    }
  }
  p
}
```

## 5.10 Linked dense heatmap (all samples in one coordinate space)

<!-- ==========================================================================
     Like plot_fiberseq_dense(), but every sample gets a horizontal "lane"
     inside ONE shared ggplot coordinate space rather than a separate patchwork
     panel. That is what makes the DMSO -> dTag cluster ribbons possible: a
     polygon cannot span two independent patchwork viewports.

     CLUSTER ROW HEIGHTS are proportional to that cluster's share of that
     sample's reads, so every lane fills the same total height regardless of
     depth -- exactly what facet_grid(scales = "free_y", space = "free_y")
     shows in plot_fiberseq_dense(). Because the shares differ between two
     linked samples, the connector is a TRAPEZOID, and its taper is the visual
     statement of how the cluster's share shifts between conditions.

     The genomic x axis is suppressed: each lane has its own local coordinate
     block, so one shared axis would be meaningless. A small "start-end" label
     is drawn under each lane instead. binding_sites and vlines are redrawn
     once per lane.
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r fn-linked}
plot_fiberseq_dense_linked <- function(plot_df, plot_range, sample_order,
                                       link_pairs = NULL,
                                       fill_color = TF_FILL,
                                       binding_sites = NULL,
                                       binding_site_alpha = 1,
                                       binding_site_linewidth = 0.6,
                                       n_label_tiers = 3,
                                       label_tier_gap = NULL,
                                       label_gap = NULL,
                                       vlines = NULL, vline_colors = NULL,
                                       link_fill = "grey50", link_alpha = 0.18,
                                       link_linetype = "22", link_color = "grey30",
                                       lane_gap_frac = 0.15,
                                       lane_height = 100,
                                       cluster_gap = 0,
                                       cluster_box = FALSE,
                                       cluster_box_color = "black",
                                       cluster_box_linewidth = 0.4,
                                       show_cluster_labels = TRUE,
                                       atac_df = NULL,          # compute_atac_signal() output
                                       atac_height = NULL,      # NULL = 10% of lane_height
                                       atac_gap = NULL,         # NULL =  5% of lane_height
                                       atac_ylim = NULL,        # NULL = shared max per scale group
                                       atac_scale_groups = NULL,# defaults to link_pairs
                                       atac_color = NULL,       # NULL = reuse fill_color
                                       atac_fill_alpha = 0.25,
                                       sample_label_gap = NULL,
                                       sample_display_labels = NULL,
                                       label_groups = NULL,
                                       group_label_gap = NULL,
                                       # decoration switches, for stacking several
                                       # panels that share one set of headers
                                       show_binding_labels = TRUE,
                                       show_lane_underline = TRUE,
                                       show_range_label = TRUE,
                                       margin_top = NULL,
                                       margin_bottom = 5,
                                       title = "Clustered Fiber-seq: linked cluster view",
                                       raster = TRUE, raster_dpi = 300,
                                       xlab = NULL) {

  chr          <- as.character(seqnames(plot_range))
  xlab         <- xlab %||% paste0("Genomic coordinate (", chr, ")")
  region_start <- start(plot_range)
  region_end   <- end(plot_range)
  region_width <- region_end - region_start + 1

  plot_df <- plot_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(Sample %in% sample_order) %>%
    mutate(Sample = factor(Sample, levels = sample_order))

  n_s       <- length(sample_order)
  gap_width <- region_width * lane_gap_frac
  lane_x0   <- setNames((seq_len(n_s) - 1) * (region_width + gap_width), sample_order)

  # ---- vertical layout, all relative to lane_height so the ATAC track, the
  #      motif label tiers and the sample name never collide -----------------
  has_atac         <- !is.null(atac_df)
  atac_gap         <- atac_gap         %||% (lane_height * 0.05)
  atac_height      <- atac_height      %||% (lane_height * 0.10)
  label_gap        <- label_gap        %||% (lane_height * 0.05)
  label_tier_gap   <- label_tier_gap   %||% (lane_height * 0.08)
  sample_label_gap <- sample_label_gap %||% (lane_height * 0.05)
  group_label_gap  <- group_label_gap  %||% (lane_height * 0.12)

  atac_top       <- if (has_atac) lane_height + atac_gap + atac_height else lane_height
  labels_base    <- atac_top + label_gap                                # tier-0 anchor
  # With show_binding_labels = FALSE there is no text above the lanes, so the
  # label tiers must not reserve their height -- otherwise a stacked panel
  # carries ~30 units of empty headroom it never uses.
  show_bs_labels <- !is.null(binding_sites) && show_binding_labels
  labels_top     <- if (show_bs_labels) {
    labels_base + (n_label_tiers - 1) * label_tier_gap                  # top tier
  } else atac_top
  sample_label_y <- labels_top + sample_label_gap
  group_label_y  <- sample_label_y + group_label_gap

  # ---- per (Sample, cluster) band geometry: share of that sample's reads ----
  band_stats <- plot_df %>%
    group_by(Sample, cluster) %>%
    summarise(n_reads = max(local_index), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(Sample) %>%
    arrange(Sample, cluster) %>%
    mutate(
      idx          = row_number(),
      n_clust      = n(),
      avail_height = lane_height - cluster_gap * (n_clust - 1),
      height       = avail_height * n_reads / sum(n_reads),
      cum_before   = dplyr::lag(cumsum(height), default = 0) + (idx - 1) * cluster_gap,
      top          = lane_height - cum_before,
      bottom       = top - height
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  # ---- one rectangle per footprint ------------------------------------------
  plot_df2 <- plot_df %>%
    left_join(band_stats %>% select(Sample, cluster, n_reads, top, bottom),
              by = c("Sample", "cluster")) %>%
    mutate(
      band_h   = top - bottom,
      y_center = bottom + (local_index - 0.5) / n_reads * band_h,
      y_half   = 0.45 / n_reads * band_h,
      x0       = lane_x0[as.character(Sample)],
      xmin     = x0 + pmax(start, region_start) - region_start,
      xmax     = x0 + pmin(end,   region_end)   - region_start,
      ymin     = y_center - y_half,
      ymax     = y_center + y_half,
      fill_hex = vapply(as.character(Sample), .resolve_fill,
                        character(1), fill_color = fill_color)
    )

  # ---- link geometry: shaded trapezoid + dashed top/bottom edges -------------
  link_polys <- NULL
  link_edges <- NULL
  if (!is.null(link_pairs) && length(link_pairs) > 0) {

    bad <- base::setdiff(unlist(link_pairs), sample_order)
    if (length(bad) > 0) {
      stop("link_pairs reference sample(s) not in sample_order: ",
           paste(bad, collapse = ", "))
    }

    link_geo <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(link_pairs), function(i) {
      sA <- link_pairs[[i]][1]; sB <- link_pairs[[i]][2]
      bA <- band_stats %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == sA)
      bB <- band_stats %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == sB)
      common <- base::intersect(as.character(bA$cluster), as.character(bB$cluster))
      if (length(common) == 0) {
        warning(sprintf("No shared clusters between '%s' and '%s'; link skipped.", sA, sB))
      }
      purrr::map_dfr(common, function(cl) {
        rA <- bA[as.character(bA$cluster) == cl, ]
        rB <- bB[as.character(bB$cluster) == cl, ]
        tibble(link_id = paste(sA, sB, cl, sep = "__"), cluster = cl,
               xA = lane_x0[sA] + region_width, xB = lane_x0[sB],
               topA = rA$top, botA = rA$bottom, topB = rB$top, botB = rB$bottom)
      })
    })

    link_polys <- purrr::pmap_dfr(link_geo, function(link_id, cluster, xA, xB,
                                                     topA, botA, topB, botB) {
      tibble(link_id = link_id, x = c(xA, xB, xB, xA), y = c(botA, botB, topB, topA))
    })
    link_edges <- bind_rows(
      link_geo %>% transmute(edge_id = paste0(link_id, "_top"),
                             x1 = xA, y1 = topA, x2 = xB, y2 = topB),
      link_geo %>% transmute(edge_id = paste0(link_id, "_bottom"),
                             x1 = xA, y1 = botA, x2 = xB, y2 = botB)
    )
  }

  p <- ggplot()

  # ---- ATAC track, drawn first so everything layers on top -------------------
  if (has_atac) {

    atac_plot_df <- atac_df %>% dplyr::filter(Sample %in% sample_order)

    # samples in the same scale group share a y maximum, so a DMSO/dTag pair is
    # visually comparable. Defaults to the link_pairs grouping.
    scale_groups <- atac_scale_groups %||% link_pairs
    group_lookup <- character(0)
    if (!is.null(scale_groups)) {
      for (i in seq_along(scale_groups)) group_lookup[scale_groups[[i]]] <- paste0("grp", i)
    }
    ungrouped <- base::setdiff(sample_order, names(group_lookup))
    group_lookup[ungrouped] <- ungrouped
    atac_plot_df$scale_group <- group_lookup[as.character(atac_plot_df$Sample)]

    if (is.null(atac_ylim)) {
      group_range <- atac_plot_df %>%
        group_by(scale_group) %>%
        summarise(y_lo = 0, y_hi = max(signal, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
      atac_plot_df <- atac_plot_df %>% left_join(group_range, by = "scale_group")
    } else {
      atac_plot_df <- atac_plot_df %>% mutate(y_lo = atac_ylim[1], y_hi = atac_ylim[2])
    }

    atac_fill_lookup <- atac_color %||% fill_color
    baseline_y       <- lane_height + atac_gap

    atac_plot_df <- atac_plot_df %>%
      mutate(
        x0       = lane_x0[as.character(Sample)],
        x        = x0 + pos - region_start,
        sig_clip = pmin(pmax(signal, y_lo), y_hi),
        y        = baseline_y + (sig_clip - y_lo) / (y_hi - y_lo) * atac_height,
        col_hex  = vapply(as.character(Sample), .resolve_fill,
                          character(1), fill_color = atac_fill_lookup)
      )

    baseline_df   <- tibble(x    = lane_x0[sample_order],
                            xend = lane_x0[sample_order] + region_width,
                            y    = baseline_y)
    atac_label_df <- tibble(x = lane_x0[sample_order] + region_width * 0.02,
                            y = atac_top, label = "ATAC")

    atac_layer <- geom_ribbon(data = atac_plot_df,
                              aes(x = x, ymin = baseline_y, ymax = y,
                                  group = Sample, fill = col_hex),
                              alpha = atac_fill_alpha, inherit.aes = FALSE)
    if (raster) atac_layer <- ggrastr::rasterise(atac_layer, dpi = raster_dpi,
                                                 dev = "ragg_png")

    p <- p +
      geom_segment(data = baseline_df, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y),
                   colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      atac_layer +
      scale_fill_identity(guide = "none") +
      geom_line(data = atac_plot_df,
                aes(x = x, y = y, group = Sample, colour = col_hex),
                linewidth = 0.4, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      scale_colour_identity(guide = "none") +
      geom_text(data = atac_label_df, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
                hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 2.3, colour = "grey40",
                fontface = "italic", inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }

  # ---- motif guides, with labels staggered across n_label_tiers ---------------
  # show_binding_labels = FALSE keeps the dashed guides but stops them at the
  # top of the lanes and draws no text, so a stacked panel can carry the
  # vertical alignment cues without repeating the motif names.
  if (!is.null(binding_sites)) {
    bs_all <- purrr::map_dfr(sample_order, function(s) {
      binding_sites %>%
        arrange(xmin) %>%
        mutate(tier     = (row_number() - 1) %% n_label_tiers,
               x_center = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
               x        = lane_x0[s] + x_center - region_start,
               label_y  = if (show_bs_labels) labels_base + tier * label_tier_gap
                          else lane_height)
    })
    p <- p +
      geom_segment(data = bs_all,
                   aes(x = x, xend = x, y = 0, yend = label_y, colour = col),
                   linetype = "dashed", linewidth = binding_site_linewidth,
                   alpha = binding_site_alpha, inherit.aes = FALSE)
    if (show_bs_labels) {
      p <- p + geom_text(data = bs_all,
                         aes(x = x, y = label_y, label = TF, colour = col),
                         vjust = -0.1, size = 2.5, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                         show.legend = FALSE)
    }
    p <- p + scale_colour_identity(guide = "none")
  }

  if (!is.null(link_polys)) {
    p <- p +
      geom_polygon(data = link_polys, aes(x = x, y = y, group = link_id),
                   fill = link_fill, alpha = link_alpha, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      geom_segment(data = link_edges, aes(x = x1, y = y1, xend = x2, yend = y2),
                   linetype = link_linetype, colour = link_color,
                   linewidth = 0.4, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }

  rect_layer <- geom_rect(data = plot_df2,
                          aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
                          fill = plot_df2$fill_hex, colour = NA)
  if (raster) rect_layer <- ggrastr::rasterise(rect_layer, dpi = raster_dpi,
                                               dev = "ragg_png")
  p <- p + rect_layer

  if (cluster_box) {
    box_df <- purrr::map_dfr(sample_order, function(s) {
      band_stats %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == s) %>%
        mutate(xmin = lane_x0[s], xmax = lane_x0[s] + region_width)
    })
    p <- p + geom_rect(data = box_df,
                       aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = bottom, ymax = top),
                       fill = NA, colour = cluster_box_color,
                       linewidth = cluster_box_linewidth, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }

  if (!is.null(vlines)) {
    if (is.null(vline_colors)) vline_colors <- rep("black", length(vlines))
    vl_df <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(vlines), function(i) {
      purrr::map_dfr(sample_order, function(s) {
        tibble(x = lane_x0[s] + vlines[i] - region_start, colour = vline_colors[i])
      })
    })
    p <- p +
      geom_segment(data = vl_df, aes(x = x, xend = x, y = 0, yend = lane_height,
                                     colour = colour),
                   linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5,
                   inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      scale_colour_identity(guide = "none")
  }

  # ---- per-lane label + underline (e.g. "DMSO" / "dTag") ---------------------
  lane_label_text <- if (!is.null(sample_display_labels)) {
    sample_display_labels[sample_order]
  } else sample_order

  # Drawing an EMPTY label still expands the y range to sample_label_y, so a
  # panel with blanked names kept its headroom. Skip the layers entirely when
  # there is nothing to show.
  if (show_lane_underline) {
    lane_underlines <- tibble(x    = lane_x0[sample_order],
                              xend = lane_x0[sample_order] + region_width,
                              y    = sample_label_y)
    p <- p + geom_segment(data = lane_underlines,
                          aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y),
                          colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  if (any(nzchar(lane_label_text))) {
    lane_labels <- tibble(x = lane_x0[sample_order] + region_width / 2,
                          y = sample_label_y, label = lane_label_text)
    p <- p + geom_text(data = lane_labels, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
                       vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }

  # ---- group label spanning several lanes ------------------------------------
  if (!is.null(label_groups)) {
    group_df <- imap_dfr(label_groups, function(members, glabel) {
      bad <- base::setdiff(members, sample_order)
      if (length(bad) > 0) {
        warning("label_groups entry '", glabel, "' references sample(s) not in ",
                "sample_order: ", paste(bad, collapse = ", "), " -- skipping.")
        return(NULL)
      }
      tibble(label = glabel,
             x0 = min(lane_x0[members]),
             x1 = max(lane_x0[members]) + region_width)
    })
    p <- p +
      geom_segment(data = group_df,
                   aes(x = x0, xend = x1, y = group_label_y, yend = group_label_y),
                   colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      geom_text(data = group_df,
                aes(x = (x0 + x1) / 2, y = group_label_y, label = label),
                vjust = -0.3, size = 3.8, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }

  # Repeated under every lane, so worth switching off on all but the bottom
  # panel of a stack.
  if (show_range_label) {
    range_labels <- tibble(x = lane_x0[sample_order] + region_width / 2, y = 0,
                           label = paste0(comma(region_start), "-", comma(region_end)))
    p <- p + geom_text(data = range_labels, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
                       vjust = 2.2, size = 2.3, colour = "grey40", inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }

  if (show_cluster_labels) {
    lbl <- band_stats %>%
      mutate(x = lane_x0[as.character(Sample)], y = (top + bottom) / 2)
    p <- p + geom_text(data = lbl, aes(x = x, y = y, label = cluster),
                       hjust = 1.3, size = 2.8, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }

  p +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(),
          plot.margin = margin(
            t = margin_top %||% (if (!is.null(label_groups)) 50
                                 else if (has_atac) 40 else 20),
            r = 5, b = margin_bottom, l = 20)) +
    labs(title = title, x = xlab, y = NULL)
}
```

## 5.11 MSP geometry and the open / closed summary

<!-- ==========================================================================
     For one enhancer, collapse the k-means clusters into "open" and "closed"
     groups and compute log2FC(dTag / DMSO) of the % of reads in each group,
     per replicate pair.

     TWO WAYS TO DEFINE THE GROUPS

       (A) MANUAL   pass open_clusters and closed_clusters as integer vectors.

       (B) AUTO     pass msp_files + motif_range. A cluster is "open" if, among
                    its MSPs overlapping the motif:
                        mean_msp_width >= min_msp_width      AND
                        width_before   >= min_width_before   AND
                        width_after    >= min_width_after    AND
                        n_msp          >= min_n_msp
                    Every other cluster becomes "closed" (the complement, so no
                    cluster is left unclassified).

     ON THE THRESHOLDS : for the same pool of overlapping
     MSPs these three widths satisfy
         mean_msp_width = width_before + width_after + motif_width
     so with a small motif and 300 / 150 / 150 the mean_msp_width test is
     already implied by the other two and adds nothing. It is kept because it
     is harmless and self-documenting, and because it would matter for a very
     asymmetric overhang. In the methods, describe the criterion as "at least
     150 bp of accessible MSP on each side of the motif".

     clusters with fewer than min_n_msp motif-overlapping
     MSPs are called "closed" by default rather than trusted on sparse data.
     The function messages which clusters this affected -- read those messages.

     The output always carries a `clusters` column recording which cluster IDs
     went into that row's group, so the result is self-documenting even though
     the classification is data-driven.
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r fn-msp}
#' Mean MSP geometry around a motif, per cluster
#'
#' @param motif_range  a GRanges, or c(start, end) plus an explicit `chrom`.
#'   MSP .bed files pool footprints from several PCR amplicons, so filtering on
#'   numeric coordinates alone can match the wrong locus -- chrom is mandatory.
compute_msp_motif_stats <- function(msp_files, cluster_assignments_perrep,
                                    motif_range, chrom = NULL) {

  if (methods::is(motif_range, "GRanges")) {
    chrom       <- as.character(seqnames(motif_range))
    motif_start <- start(motif_range)
    motif_end   <- end(motif_range)
  } else {
    if (is.null(chrom)) {
      stop("compute_msp_motif_stats: provide `chrom` (or pass motif_range as a ",
           "GRanges). MSP bed files pool multiple amplicons, so filtering on ",
           "coordinates alone risks matching the wrong locus.")
    }
    motif_start <- motif_range[1]
    motif_end   <- motif_range[2]
  }

  # FIX B1: this used to re-read the file with readLines() and attach chrom by
  #         ROW POSITION. read_fiberhmm_bed() drops malformed rows, so one bad
  #         line shifted every chromosome assignment after it -- silently
  #         corrupting the amplicon filter and therefore the open/closed call.
  #         read_fiberhmm_bed() now carries `chrom` through directly.
  msps <- imap_dfr(msp_files, function(path, s_name) {
    read_fiberhmm_bed(path)$footprints %>%
      transmute(unique_id = paste0(s_name, "_", read_name),
                chrom, msp_start = fp_start, msp_end = fp_end)
  })

  target_chrom <- chrom
  stats <- msps %>%
    dplyr::filter(chrom == target_chrom,
                  msp_end >= motif_start, msp_start <= motif_end) %>%
    inner_join(cluster_assignments_perrep %>% dplyr::select(unique_id, cluster),
               by = "unique_id") %>%
    mutate(msp_width    = msp_end - msp_start + 1L,
           width_before = motif_start - msp_start,   # accessible bp 5' of motif
           width_after  = msp_end - motif_end) %>%   # accessible bp 3' of motif
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    summarise(mean_msp_width = mean(msp_width),
              width_before   = mean(width_before),
              width_after    = mean(width_after),
              n_msp          = dplyr::n(),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(cluster = as.integer(as.character(cluster)))

  # keep clusters with zero overlapping MSPs as explicit NA rows
  all_clusters <- sort(unique(as.integer(as.character(cluster_assignments_perrep$cluster))))
  tibble(cluster = all_clusters) %>% left_join(stats, by = "cluster")
}
```

```{r fn-openclosed}
compute_openclosed_log2fc <- function(cluster_assignments_perrep,
                                      comparisons,
                                      enhancer_name,
                                      open_clusters    = NULL,
                                      closed_clusters  = NULL,
                                      msp_files        = NULL,
                                      motif_range      = NULL,
                                      chrom            = NULL,
                                      min_msp_width    = 300,
                                      min_width_before = 150,
                                      min_width_after  = 150,
                                      min_n_msp        = 20) {

  manual_mode <- !is.null(open_clusters) || !is.null(closed_clusters)
  auto_mode   <- !is.null(msp_files)     || !is.null(motif_range)

  if (manual_mode && auto_mode) {
    stop("Provide EITHER open_clusters/closed_clusters (manual) OR ",
         "msp_files/motif_range (auto), not both.")
  }
  if (!manual_mode && !auto_mode) {
    stop("Provide either open_clusters & closed_clusters, or msp_files & motif_range.")
  }
  if (manual_mode && (is.null(open_clusters) || is.null(closed_clusters))) {
    stop("Manual mode requires BOTH open_clusters and closed_clusters.")
  }
  if (auto_mode && (is.null(msp_files) || is.null(motif_range))) {
    stop("Auto mode requires BOTH msp_files and motif_range.")
  }

  if (auto_mode) {
    msp_stats    <- compute_msp_motif_stats(msp_files, cluster_assignments_perrep,
                                            motif_range, chrom = chrom)
    all_clusters <- sort(unique(as.integer(as.character(cluster_assignments_perrep$cluster))))

    is_open <- !is.na(msp_stats$mean_msp_width) & msp_stats$mean_msp_width >= min_msp_width &
               !is.na(msp_stats$width_before)   & msp_stats$width_before   >= min_width_before &
               !is.na(msp_stats$width_after)    & msp_stats$width_after    >= min_width_after &
               !is.na(msp_stats$n_msp)          & msp_stats$n_msp          >= min_n_msp

    open_clusters   <- as.integer(as.character(msp_stats$cluster[is_open]))
    closed_clusters <- base::setdiff(all_clusters, open_clusters)

    message(sprintf("[%s] auto-classified from MSP geometry: open = {%s}, closed = {%s}",
                    enhancer_name,
                    paste(sort(open_clusters),   collapse = ","),
                    paste(sort(closed_clusters), collapse = ",")))

    low_n <- msp_stats$cluster[!is.na(msp_stats$n_msp) & msp_stats$n_msp < min_n_msp]
    if (length(low_n) > 0) {
      message("  note: cluster(s) ", paste(sort(low_n), collapse = ","),
              " had < ", min_n_msp, " motif-overlapping MSPs -- called 'closed' ",
              "by default rather than trusted on sparse data (see Q6).")
    }
  }

  ca <- cluster_assignments_perrep %>%
    mutate(group = case_when(
      as.integer(as.character(cluster)) %in% open_clusters   ~ "open",
      as.integer(as.character(cluster)) %in% closed_clusters ~ "closed",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(group))

  # denominator = ALL reads in that sample. In auto mode open + closed is the
  # complete set, so this is the same thing. In manual mode with unassigned
  # clusters it is NOT -- the percentages will not sum to 100.
  total_per_sample <- cluster_assignments_perrep %>%
    dplyr::count(Sample, name = "total_reads")

  pct_wide <- ca %>%
    dplyr::count(Sample, group, name = "n_reads") %>%
    left_join(total_per_sample, by = "Sample") %>%
    mutate(percent = 100 * n_reads / total_reads) %>%
    select(Sample, group, percent) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Sample, values_from = percent, values_fill = 0)

  result <- imap_dfr(comparisons, function(pair, label) {

    num <- pair[["numerator"]]
    den <- pair[["denominator"]]

    missing <- base::setdiff(c(num, den), names(pct_wide))
    if (length(missing) > 0) {
      stop("compute_openclosed_log2fc: sample(s) not found: ",
           paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
    }

    # Q4: the degraded TF is inferred from the numerator's sample name.
    # Warn rather than silently defaulting everything unmatched to SNAI.
    tf_lab <- if (grepl("TWIST1", num)) "TWIST1" else if (grepl("SNAI", num)) "SNAI" else {
      warning("Numerator '", num, "' matches neither TWIST1 nor SNAI; labelling SNAI.")
      "SNAI"
    }

    tibble(
      enhancer       = enhancer_name,
      Replicate_Pair = label,
      TF             = tf_lab,
      group          = pct_wide$group,
      Log2Ratio      = log2(pct_wide[[num]] / pct_wide[[den]])
    )
  })

  cluster_str      <- c(open   = paste(sort(open_clusters),   collapse = ","),
                        closed = paste(sort(closed_clusters), collapse = ","))
  result$clusters  <- cluster_str[result$group]
  result
}
```

## 5.12 Convenience wrappers used by the per-enhancer sections

```{r fn-wrappers}
#' Build bundles, merge replicates, cluster, and split back out -- cached.
#'
#' Returns list(bundles, bundles_merged, ca_merged, ca_perrep).
#' `cache_name` becomes <ROBJ_DIR>/<cache_name>.rds
run_clustering <- function(key, samples, cluster_range, k, cache_name,
                           rebuild = REBUILD_CLUSTERS) {

  out <- cache_rds(cache_name, {
    files   <- enh_files(key, samples, "footprint")
    bundles <- build_all_bundles(files, cluster_range)

    merged     <- merge_replicate_bundles(bundles, merge_groups_for(samples))
    ca_merged  <- cluster_reads(merged, k = k, seed = KMEANS_SEED)
    ca_perrep  <- split_cluster_assignments(ca_merged)

    list(bundles        = bundles,
         bundles_merged = merged,
         ca_merged      = ca_merged,
         ca_perrep      = ca_perrep,
         kmeans_info    = attr(ca_merged, "kmeans_info"),
         meta           = list(key = key, k = k, seed = KMEANS_SEED,
                               minset = ENH[[key]]$minset,
                               cluster_range = as.character(cluster_range),
                               samples = samples,
                               R_version = R.version.string,
                               run_date  = Sys.Date()))
  }, rebuild = rebuild)

  # Print the fit quality every time, cached or not. Two things to watch:
  # a cluster with very few reads is not a real class, and a low prop_between
  # means the partition is not carrying much of the variance.
  ki <- out$kmeans_info
  if (!is.null(ki)) {
    message(sprintf(
      "  %s (%s): %s reads x %d bp, k = %d\n    init: %s\n    tot.withinss = %s | between/total = %.3f | %d iterations\n    cluster sizes: %s",
      enh_label(key), cache_name, format(ki$n_reads, big.mark = ","),
      ki$n_positions, ki$k, ki$init_method,
      format(round(ki$tot_withinss), big.mark = ","),
      ki$prop_between, ki$iterations,
      paste(ki$cluster_sizes, collapse = ", ")))
    tiny <- which(ki$cluster_sizes < 0.01 * ki$n_reads)
    if (length(tiny) > 0) {
      warning(enh_label(key), ": cluster(s) ", paste(tiny, collapse = ", "),
              " hold under 1% of reads. Consider a smaller k.")
    }
  }
  out
}

#' The linked DMSO/dTag heatmap, with LINKED_STYLE applied.
#' `pairs` is a named list: "group label" = c(DMSO sample, dTag sample).
linked_heatmap <- function(plot_df_merged, plot_range, pairs, atac_df,
                           binding_sites, title, fill_color = TF_FILL) {

  sample_order <- unlist(pairs, use.names = FALSE)

  do.call(plot_fiberseq_dense_linked, c(
    list(
      plot_df               = plot_df_merged,
      plot_range            = plot_range,
      sample_order          = sample_order,
      atac_df               = atac_df,
      link_pairs            = unname(pairs),
      sample_display_labels = setNames(
        ifelse(grepl("DMSO", sample_order), "DMSO", "dTag"), sample_order),
      label_groups          = pairs,
      fill_color            = fill_color,
      binding_sites         = binding_sites,
      title                 = title
    ),
    LINKED_STYLE
  ))
}

#' TF metaplot for one condition pair, replicate-averaged
tf_panel <- function(meta_avg, plot_range, tf, binding_sites, title) {
  samples <- paste0(tf, c("_DMSO", "_dTag"))
  plot_tf_metaplot_overall(
    meta_avg, plot_range,
    samples       = samples,
    sample_colors = META_COLORS[samples],
    binding_sites = binding_sites,
    subtitle      = "",
    title         = title
  )
}
```

## 5.13 Cluster stability check (opt-in)

<!-- ==========================================================================
     WHY THIS EXISTS

     Two runs of the previous pipeline differing ONLY in the order the bundles
     were stacked (same reads, same k, same seed) disagreed on 11.4% of reads
     at Enh 1: one cluster dissolved entirely and another was assembled from
     thirds of three others. nstart = 25 was not finding a stable optimum.

     The canonical row order in cluster_reads() makes a run reproducible, but
     reproducible is not the same as stable -- it only guarantees you get the
     SAME answer every time. This chunk asks the harder question: does the
     partition survive changing the seed?

     HOW TO READ IT
       ARI >= 0.9   the partition is a property of the data; k is supportable
       ARI 0.7-0.9  broadly stable, but expect some clusters to shuffle
       ARI < 0.7    the partition is substantially an artefact of the seed.
                    Do not rest a claim on individual cluster identities at
                    this k -- either lower k, or report only the pooled
                    open/closed split, which is far more robust than the
                    individual clusters because it collapses exactly the
                    boundaries that are moving.

     Clusters a fixed subsample so every seed sees identical rows. This is a
     diagnostic, not the analysis. Set eval = TRUE to run it; it is slow.
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r cluster-stability, eval = FALSE}
#' Recluster the same reads under several seeds and report pairwise agreement
cluster_stability <- function(bundles, k, seeds = c(1, 42, 123, 2024, 7),
                              subsample = 20000L) {

  mat <- do.call(rbind, map(bundles, bundle_to_matrix))
  mat <- mat[order(rownames(mat), method = "radix"), , drop = FALSE]

  if (!is.null(subsample) && nrow(mat) > subsample) {
    set.seed(1L)                                   # same rows for every seed
    mat <- mat[sort(sample.int(nrow(mat), subsample)), , drop = FALSE]
  }

  fits <- purrr::map(seeds, function(s) {
    set.seed(s)
    kmeans(mat, centers = k, nstart = KMEANS_NSTART, iter.max = KMEANS_ITER_MAX)
  })
  names(fits) <- paste0("seed", seeds)

  pairs <- utils::combn(seq_along(seeds), 2)
  ari   <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(ncol(pairs)), function(i) {
    a <- pairs[1, i]; b <- pairs[2, i]
    tibble(seed_a = seeds[a], seed_b = seeds[b],
           ARI    = adjusted_rand(fits[[a]]$cluster, fits[[b]]$cluster))
  })

  wss <- purrr::map_dbl(fits, "tot.withinss")
  list(
    ari      = ari,
    withinss = wss,
    summary  = tibble(k = k, n = nrow(mat),
                      mean_ARI = mean(ari$ARI),
                      min_ARI  = min(ari$ARI),
                      withinss_cv = sd(wss) / mean(wss))
  )
}

# Enh 1 at the k actually used
stab <- cluster_stability(enh1$bundles_merged, k = ENH$enh4$k)
print(stab$summary)
print(stab$ari)

# Sweep k, to see whether a coarser partition is better determined
sweep_k <- purrr::map_dfr(c(4, 6, 8, 10, 12), function(kk) {
  cluster_stability(enh1$bundles_merged, k = kk, seeds = c(1, 42, 123))$summary
})
print(sweep_k)
```

# 6. Per-enhancer analyses

<!-- ==========================================================================
     Each section follows the same shape:
       (a) cluster        run_clustering() -> bundles / merged / assignments
       (b) heatmap        linked_heatmap() + make_log2fc_panel()
       (c) open/closed    compute_openclosed_log2fc(), assigned to a NAMED
                          object (never appended to a global -- see C4)
       (d) TF metaplots   build_tf_metaplot_data() -> compute_tf_metaplot()

     Every title and filename comes from enh_label() / fig_name(), so the paper
     names in section 3 are the single source of truth.
     ========================================================================== -->

### 6.2.4 Enh 2: opening across the three peaks

```{r enh2-peak-summary, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 3}
peak_levels <- c("Enh 2 peak 1", "Enh 2 peak 2", "Enh 2 peak 3")

df_plot <- bind_rows(enh2_peak1_summary, enh2_peak2_summary, enh2_peak3_summary) %>%
  dplyr::filter(group == "open") %>%
  mutate(
    enhancer    = factor(enhancer, levels = peak_levels),
    peak_label  = sub("^Enh 2 ", "", as.character(enhancer)),
    TF          = factor(TF, levels = c("TWIST1", "SNAI")),
    facet_label = factor(ifelse(TF == "TWIST1", "TWIST1 depletion", "SNAI1/2 depletion"),
                         levels = c("SNAI1/2 depletion", "TWIST1 depletion"))
  )

df_mean <- df_plot %>%
  group_by(enhancer, peak_label, TF, facet_label) %>%
  summarise(mean_log2fc = mean(Log2Ratio, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

p_enh2_peaks <- ggplot(df_mean, aes(x = peak_label, y = mean_log2fc, fill = TF)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6,
           colour = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  # FIX B6: geom_point has no `linewidth`; the outline width is `stroke`
  geom_point(data = df_plot, aes(x = peak_label, y = Log2Ratio, fill = TF),
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
             shape = 21, size = 1.5, colour = "black", stroke = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = TF_FILL) +
  facet_wrap(~ facet_label, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, fill = NULL,
       y = "log2(dTag/DMSO) of % reads in accessible clusters (+/- 150 bp of motif)") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position  = "none",
        axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"))

p_enh2_peaks
ggsave(fig_name(key, "openclosed_by_peak"), p_enh2_peaks,
       width = 4, height = 3, device = cairo_pdf)
```

### 6.2.5 Enh 2: all three peak clusterings in one stacked figure

<!-- ==========================================================================
     The same reads and the same window drawn three times, clustered on a
     different peak each time: peak 1 (TWIST1) top, peak 2 (SNAI) middle,
     peak 3 (E-box) bottom.

     ATAC track, motif names, lane names and the DMSO/dTag group bars appear on
     the TOP panel only. The lower two keep the dashed motif guides so the eye
     can carry a vertical line down all three blocks, but with the label text
     blanked.

     Alignment: all three panels use the same plot_range and the same
     sample_order, so lane_x0 is identical and the columns line up exactly.
     Nothing here needs a new function -- it is the existing linked heatmap
     called three times with different decoration.

     The decoration is controlled by three switches on
     plot_fiberseq_dense_linked(): show_binding_labels, show_lane_underline and
     show_range_label, plus margin_top / margin_bottom. All default to the old
     behaviour, so no other figure changes. Turning the labels off also
     RECLAIMS their space -- an empty label still expanded the y range, so the
     lower blocks used to carry ~30 units of unused headroom each.
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r enh2-stacked-peaks, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 18}
key         <- "enh10"
stack_range <- enh_gr(key, "plot")

stack_pairs <- list(
  "SNAI1/2 depletion" = c("SNAI_DMSO_5min",   "SNAI_dTag_5min"),
  "TWIST1 depletion"  = c("TWIST1_DMSO_5min", "TWIST1_dTag_5min")
)
stack_order <- unlist(stack_pairs, use.names = FALSE)
stack_atac  <- compute_atac_signal(atac_for(stack_order), stack_range)

stack_motifs <- enh_motifs(key, "motifs")

#' One block of the stack.
#' @param clust  a run_clustering() result (enh2p1 / enh2p2 / enh2p3)
#' @param decorate TRUE only for the top block: ATAC, motif names, lane names,
#'   DMSO/dTag group bars. The lower blocks keep the dashed motif guides for
#'   vertical alignment but draw no header at all.
#' @param show_xlab TRUE only for the bottom block
stack_block <- function(clust, title, decorate = FALSE, show_xlab = FALSE) {

  pdf_merged <- prepare_plot_data(clust$bundles_merged, clust$ca_merged, stack_range)

  do.call(plot_fiberseq_dense_linked, c(
    list(
      plot_df       = pdf_merged,
      plot_range    = stack_range,
      sample_order  = stack_order,
      link_pairs    = unname(stack_pairs),
      fill_color    = TF_FILL,
      title         = title,
      binding_sites = stack_motifs,
      atac_df       = if (decorate) stack_atac  else NULL,
      label_groups  = if (decorate) stack_pairs else NULL,
      sample_display_labels = if (decorate) {
        setNames(ifelse(grepl("DMSO", stack_order), "DMSO", "dTag"), stack_order)
      } else NULL,

      # header drawn once, on the top block only
      show_binding_labels = decorate,   # guides stay, motif names do not
      show_lane_underline = decorate,   # the bare black rule above the lanes
      # the coordinate caption is identical in all 12 lanes -- bottom row only
      show_range_label    = show_xlab,

      # blocks 2 and 3 need no headroom, so pull them up under the one above
      margin_top    = if (decorate) NULL else 2,
      margin_bottom = if (show_xlab) 5 else 0,

      # "" is not NULL, so %||% leaves it alone and the axis title is blank
      xlab = if (show_xlab) NULL else ""
    ),
    LINKED_STYLE
  ))
}

p_peak1 <- stack_block(enh2p1, "Clustered on peak 1 (TWIST1 motif)", decorate = TRUE)
p_peak2 <- stack_block(enh2p2, "Clustered on peak 2 (SNAI1/2 motif)")
p_peak3 <- stack_block(enh2p3, "Clustered on peak 3 (E-box)", show_xlab = TRUE)

# Top block is taller because it alone carries the ATAC track, the motif names
# and the group bars. Blocks 2 and 3 now occupy almost exactly their lane
# height, so 1.35 / 1 / 1 keeps the three read blocks the same physical size.
p_enh2_stack <- (p_peak1 / p_peak2 / p_peak3) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1.35, 1, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(title = enh_label(key))

p_enh2_stack
ggsave(fig_name(key, "heatmap_linked_all3peaks_stacked"), p_enh2_stack,
       width = 10, height = 15, limitsize = FALSE, device = cairo_pdf)
```

```{r enh2-stacked-peaks-with-fc, eval = FALSE, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 18}
# Variant: same stack with the per-cluster log2FC bars alongside each block.
# Each row is (heatmap | SNAI bars | TWIST1 bars); patchwork nests fine.
fc_pair <- function(clust) {
  d <- compute_log2fc_df(clust$ca_perrep, comparisons_5min)
  (make_log2fc_panel(d %>% dplyr::filter(grepl("SNAI",   Replicate_Pair)),
                     title = "SNAI",   palette = snai_palette,  xlim = c(-0.8, 0.8)) |
   make_log2fc_panel(d %>% dplyr::filter(grepl("TWIST1", Replicate_Pair)),
                     title = "TWIST1", palette = twist_palette, xlim = c(-2, 2)))
}

row1 <- (p_peak1 | fc_pair(enh2p1)) + plot_layout(widths = c(5, 2))
row2 <- (p_peak2 | fc_pair(enh2p2)) + plot_layout(widths = c(5, 2))
row3 <- (p_peak3 | fc_pair(enh2p3)) + plot_layout(widths = c(5, 2))

p_enh2_stack_fc <- (row1 / row2 / row3) + plot_layout(heights = c(1.35, 1, 1))
ggsave(fig_name(key, "heatmap_linked_all3peaks_stacked_withFC"), p_enh2_stack_fc,
       width = 14, height = 18, limitsize = FALSE, device = cairo_pdf)
```

## 6.3 SNAI1/2-only enhancers (Enh 3, Enh 4, Enh 5, Enh 6)

<!-- These four are analysed with the SNAI1/2 degron samples only, so they all
     share one comparison set and one two-lane heatmap layout. -->

```{r snai-only-common}
comparisons_snai <- list(
  "Rep1" = c(numerator = "SNAI_rep1_dTag5min", denominator = "SNAI_rep1_DMSO5min"),
  "Rep2" = c(numerator = "SNAI_rep2_dTag5min", denominator = "SNAI_rep2_DMSO5min")
)

# open/closed summaries use the same two pairs but labelled for the figure
comparisons_snai_oc <- list(
  "SNAI R1 5m (dTag/DMSO)" = c(numerator = "SNAI_rep1_dTag5min", denominator = "SNAI_rep1_DMSO5min"),
  "SNAI R2 5m (dTag/DMSO)" = c(numerator = "SNAI_rep2_dTag5min", denominator = "SNAI_rep2_DMSO5min")
)

pairs_snai   <- list("SNAI1/2 depletion" = c("SNAI_DMSO_5min", "SNAI_dTag_5min"))
order_snai   <- unlist(pairs_snai, use.names = FALSE)

#' Heatmap + log2FC bar for a two-lane SNAI-only enhancer
snai_heatmap_panel <- function(clust, key, peak = NULL, plot_range,
                               title, fc_xlim = NULL) {

  atac_df        <- compute_atac_signal(atac_for(order_snai), plot_range)
  plot_df_merged <- prepare_plot_data(clust$bundles_merged, clust$ca_merged, plot_range)
  log2fc_df      <- compute_log2fc_df(clust$ca_perrep, comparisons_snai)

  p_heat <- linked_heatmap(plot_df_merged, plot_range,
                           pairs         = pairs_snai,
                           atac_df       = atac_df,
                           binding_sites = enh_motifs(key, "motifs", peak = peak),
                           title         = title,
                           fill_color    = c(SNAI = "darkred"))

  p_bar <- make_log2fc_panel(log2fc_df, title = "log2FC",
                             palette = snai_palette, xlim = fc_xlim) +
    theme(legend.position = "right")

  (p_heat | p_bar) + plot_layout(widths = c(5, 1))
}

#' All-reads vs accessible-reads TF metaplots + ATAC, for a SNAI-only enhancer
snai_tf_figure <- function(clust, key, tf_range, cache_tag,
                           accessible = enh_accessible(key)) {

  tf_bs <- enh_motifs(key, "motifs_tf")

  tf_df <- cache_rds(
    sprintf("tf_df_%s_thr%dw%d", cache_tag, TF_SCORE_THR, TF_MAX_WIDTH),
    build_tf_metaplot_data(enh_files(key, only(SNAI_SAMPLES, "1min"), "tf"),
                           clust$ca_perrep, tf_range,
                           score_threshold = TF_SCORE_THR, max_width = TF_MAX_WIDTH)
  )

  tf_all <- compute_tf_metaplot(tf_df, clust$ca_perrep, tf_range,
                                bundles = clust$bundles, pool_clusters = TRUE) %>%
    average_replicates()
  tf_acc <- compute_tf_metaplot(tf_df, clust$ca_perrep, tf_range,
                                bundles = clust$bundles, clusters = accessible,
                                pool_clusters = TRUE) %>%
    average_replicates()

  p1 <- tf_panel(tf_all, tf_range, "SNAI", tf_bs, enh_label(key, "- all reads"))
  p2 <- tf_panel(tf_acc, tf_range, "SNAI", tf_bs,
                 enh_label(key, paste0("- cluster ", paste(accessible, collapse = ","))))
  p_atac <- plot_atac_signal(compute_atac_signal(ATAC_BW["SNAI_DMSO"], tf_range),
                             tf_range, binding_sites = tf_bs, title = enh_label(key))

  ggarrange(p_atac, p1, p2, nrow = 3, align = "hv", legend = "right",
            heights = c(0.7, 1, 1))
}
```

## 7.1 Assemble the open/closed table

```{r summary-assemble}
open_closed_all <- bind_rows(
  enh1_summary_snai,    # Enh 1, SNAI motif
```

## 7.2 Chromatin opening on TF degradation, one bar per enhancer

<!-- Each enhancer contributes the peak where the degraded TF actually binds:
       Enh 1  both motifs (SNAI + TWIST1) were quantified
       Enh 2  TWIST1 read out at peak 1, SNAI1/2 read out at peak 2
       Enh 3  the SNAI1/2 peak (peak 1)
       Enh 4-6  their single SNAI1/2 peak -->

```{r summary-plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
plot_open_summary <- function(summary_df, enhancer_order, ylim = NULL,
                              tf_colors = TF_FILL) {

  df <- summary_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(group == "open") %>%
    mutate(enhancer = factor(enhancer, levels = enhancer_order))

  df_mean <- df %>%
    group_by(enhancer, TF) %>%
    summarise(mean_log2fc = mean(Log2Ratio, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  p <- ggplot(df_mean, aes(x = enhancer, y = mean_log2fc, fill = TF)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6,
             colour = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_point(data = df, aes(x = enhancer, y = Log2Ratio, fill = TF),
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
               shape = 21, size = 1.5, colour = "black", stroke = 0.2) +  # FIX B6
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, colour = "black") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = tf_colors) +
    labs(x = "Enhancer", fill = NULL,
         y = "log2(dTag/DMSO) of % reads in accessible clusters (+/- 150 bp of motif)") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(legend.position = "right",
          axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

  if (!is.null(ylim)) p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim)
  p
}

summary_subset <- open_closed_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    (enhancer == "Enh 2 peak 1" & TF == "TWIST1") |     # TWIST1 at its own peak
    (enhancer == "Enh 2 peak 2" & TF == "SNAI")   |     # SNAI1/2 at its own peak
    enhancer %in% c("Enh 1", "Enh 3 peak 1", "Enh 4", "Enh 5", "Enh 6")
  ) %>%
  mutate(enhancer = recode(enhancer,
                           "Enh 2 peak 1" = "Enh 2",
                           "Enh 2 peak 2" = "Enh 2",
                           "Enh 3 peak 1" = "Enh 3"))

p_open <- plot_open_summary(
  summary_subset,
  enhancer_order = c("Enh 1", "Enh 2", "Enh 3", "Enh 4", "Enh 5", "Enh 6")
)
p_open
ggsave(fig("summary_open_closed_all_enhancers_v297.pdf"), p_open,
       width = 6, height = 4)
```

## 7.3 TF footprint occupancy: all reads vs accessible reads (CMH)

<!-- ==========================================================================
     SNAI1/2 DMSO vs dTag, 1 min DAF. Plotted: TFAP2A at Enh 2, TFAP2A at
     Enh 5, NR2F1 at Enh 5. The Enh 1 and Enh 6 sites are kept commented out in
     `sites` below; enh_config covers all four enhancers.

     LAYOUT  facet_grid(read_set ~ site), row 1 = all reads, row 2 = accessible
             reads, scales = "free_y" so each ROW gets its own y axis.

     OCCUPANCY (the bars)  same definition as plot_tf_metaplot_overall():
             per bp   -> TF footprints covering bp / read coverage at bp * 100
             per site -> mean of that over the motif's bp (bp below
                         min_read_cov are NA and excluded)

     READ SETS
       All reads        compute_tf_metaplot(pool_clusters = TRUE): denominator
                        is every read of that sample.
       Accessible reads compute_tf_metaplot(clusters = <open set>,
                        pool_clusters = TRUE): numerator AND denominator are
                        restricted to that enhancer's open cluster(s), the same
                        sets used in the per-enhancer TF metaplots above.

     STATISTICS
       Plotted: Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel on per-read footprint calls, stratified
         by replicate. For every read FULLY spanning the motif, "is there a TF
         footprint overlapping the motif?" -> 2 x 2 x 2 table
         (condition x footprinted x replicate). Note this tests the PERCENTAGE
         OF READS footprinted -- a per-molecule quantity, close to but not
         identical to the mean per-bp occupancy drawn as the bars. Both appear
         in the QC table.
       Printed only: paired t-test on the per-replicate occupancy values shown
         as points. n = 2 pairs, df = 1 

     Self-contained: reloads the cached clustering objects and the SNAI 1-min
     tf .bed files itself, so it only needs sections 1-5 to have been run.
     ========================================================================== -->

```{r cmh-config}
# Each enhancer must be paired with the tf .bed set matching the fiberHMM call
# set it was CLUSTERED on -- Enh 1 is min1, the rest are min3 (reviewer note Q1).
enh_config <- list(
  enh4  = list(cache = "enh4_k12",         accessible = enh_accessible("enh4")),
  # TFAP2A sits inside the peak-2 window, so the SNAI-centred peak-2 clustering
  # is the correct local accessibility call for it.
  enh10 = list(cache = "enh10peak2_k10",   accessible = enh_accessible("enh10", "peak2")),
  enh30 = list(cache = "ENH30_k10",        accessible = enh_accessible("enh30")),
  enh33 = list(cache = "ENH33_k10",        accessible = enh_accessible("enh33"))
)

# TF sites to quantify.
#   NR2F1 at Enh 5 = the two adjacent motifs treated as one window.
#   TFAP2A at Enh 6 = the site closest to the SNAI motif (8,709,103-8,709,110).
sites <- tribble(
  ~enh,     ~TF,       ~motif_start, ~motif_end,
  "enh10",  "TFAP2A",      12319535,   12319546,
  "enh30",  "TFAP2A",      69117131,   69117141,
  "enh30",  "NR2F1",       69117159,   69117175
# "enh4",   "TWIST1",      17169866,   17169882,
# "enh33",  "TFAP2A",       8709060,    8709071,
# "enh33",  "TWIST1",       8709132,    8709147
)

flank           <- 300L    # bp added around the motif(s) when building tf_df;
                           # only the motif bp are averaged
read_set_levels <- c("All reads", "Accessible reads")
```

```{r cmh-per-read-calls}
#' Per-read footprint calls: the numerator/denominator for the CMH test
#'
#' denominator = reads FULLY spanning the motif (a read stopping inside the
#'               motif cannot be scored), optionally restricted to `clusters`
#' numerator   = those reads carrying a TF footprint overlapping the motif
per_read_calls <- function(tf_df_e, ca_e, bundles_e, tf_files,
                           motif_start, motif_end, clusters = NULL) {

  reads <- reads_with_clusters(bundles_e, ca_e) %>%
    dplyr::filter(Sample %in% names(tf_files),
                  read_start <= motif_start, read_end >= motif_end)

  if (!is.null(clusters)) {
    reads <- reads %>%
      dplyr::filter(as.character(cluster) %in% as.character(clusters))
  }

  fp_ids <- tf_df_e %>%
    dplyr::filter(start <= motif_end, end >= motif_start) %>%
    dplyr::pull(unique_id) %>% unique()

  reads %>%
    transmute(Sample, unique_id,
              footprinted = factor(ifelse(unique_id %in% fp_ids, "yes", "no"),
                                   levels = c("yes", "no")))
}
```

```{r cmh-quantify}
res <- purrr::map(unique(sites$enh), function(enh_key) {

  cfg      <- enh_config[[enh_key]]
  enh_site <- sites %>% dplyr::filter(enh == enh_key)
  lab      <- enh_label(enh_key)

  message("=== ", enh_key, " -> ", lab, " ===")

  clust     <- readRDS(robj(paste0(cfg$cache, ".rds")))
  bundles_e <- clust$bundles
  ca_e      <- clust$ca_perrep
  tf_files  <- enh_files(enh_key, only(SNAI_SAMPLES, "1min"), "tf")

  # one window covering every site of this enhancer, plus flank
  win <- GRanges(ENH[[enh_key]]$chrom,
                 IRanges(min(enh_site$motif_start) - flank,
                         max(enh_site$motif_end)   + flank))

  tf_df_e <- cache_rds(
    sprintf("tf_df_occbar_%s_thr%dw%d", enh_key, TF_SCORE_THR, TF_MAX_WIDTH),
    build_tf_metaplot_data(tf_files, ca_e, win,
                           score_threshold = TF_SCORE_THR,
                           max_width       = TF_MAX_WIDTH)
  )

  # per-bp occupancy for the two read sets (replicates kept separate)
  meta <- bind_rows(
    compute_tf_metaplot(tf_df_e, ca_e, win, bundles = bundles_e,
                        pool_clusters = TRUE, min_read_cov = MIN_READ_COV) %>%
      mutate(read_set = "All reads"),
    compute_tf_metaplot(tf_df_e, ca_e, win, bundles = bundles_e,
                        clusters      = cfg$accessible,
                        pool_clusters = TRUE, min_read_cov = MIN_READ_COV) %>%
      mutate(read_set = "Accessible reads")
  )

  # (a) bars: mean per-bp occupancy over each motif window, per sample
  occ <- purrr::pmap_dfr(enh_site, function(enh, TF, motif_start, motif_end) {
    meta %>%
      dplyr::filter(pos >= motif_start, pos <= motif_end) %>%
      group_by(Sample, read_set) %>%
      summarise(occupancy  = mean(normalized_occupancy, na.rm = TRUE),
                mean_depth = mean(read_coverage),
                n_bp_used  = sum(!is.na(normalized_occupancy)),
                .groups    = "drop") %>%
      mutate(enh = enh, TF = TF, fig_label = lab,
             motif = sprintf("%s:%d-%d", ENH[[enh_key]]$chrom, motif_start, motif_end),
             acc_clusters = paste(cfg$accessible, collapse = ","))
  })

  # (b) per-read calls for the CMH test
  calls <- purrr::pmap_dfr(enh_site, function(enh, TF, motif_start, motif_end) {
    bind_rows(
      per_read_calls(tf_df_e, ca_e, bundles_e, tf_files,
                     motif_start, motif_end, clusters = NULL) %>%
        mutate(read_set = "All reads"),
      per_read_calls(tf_df_e, ca_e, bundles_e, tf_files,
                     motif_start, motif_end, clusters = cfg$accessible) %>%
        mutate(read_set = "Accessible reads")
    ) %>%
      mutate(enh = enh, TF = TF, fig_label = lab)
  })

  list(occ = occ, calls = calls)
})

add_keys <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      condition  = factor(ifelse(grepl("DMSO", Sample), "DMSO", "dTag"),
                          levels = c("DMSO", "dTag")),
      replicate  = ifelse(grepl("rep1", Sample), "Rep 1", "Rep 2"),
      site_label = factor(
        paste0(TF, "\n", fig_label),
        levels = unique(paste0(sites$TF, "\n",
                               purrr::map_chr(sites$enh, enh_label)))),
      read_set   = factor(read_set, levels = read_set_levels)
    )
}

occ_df   <- purrr::map_dfr(res, "occ")   %>% add_keys()
calls_df <- purrr::map_dfr(res, "calls") %>% add_keys()
```

```{r cmh-stats}
# ---- plotted: Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel, strata = replicates ------------------
cmh_one <- function(df) {
  tab <- df %>%
    dplyr::count(replicate, condition, footprinted, name = "n") %>%
    tidyr::complete(replicate, condition, footprinted, fill = list(n = 0L))
  arr  <- stats::xtabs(n ~ condition + footprinted + replicate, data = tab)
  # drop strata with an empty margin -- mantelhaen.test cannot use them
  keep <- apply(arr, 3, function(m) all(rowSums(m) > 0) && all(colSums(m) > 0))
  arr  <- arr[, , keep, drop = FALSE]
  if (dim(arr)[3] < 1) return(NA_real_)
  tryCatch(stats::mantelhaen.test(arr, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
           error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

p_cmh <- calls_df %>%
  group_by(site_label, read_set) %>%
  group_modify(~ tibble(n_reads = nrow(.x), p_value = cmh_one(.x))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(test = "CMH on per-read footprint calls (strata = replicates)")

# ---- printed only: paired t-test on the per-replicate occupancy values ------
# n = 2 pairs, df = 1. See reviewer note Q8: do not promote these to a figure.
p_paired_t <- occ_df %>%
  select(site_label, read_set, replicate, condition, occupancy) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = occupancy) %>%
  group_by(site_label, read_set) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pairs = sum(!is.na(DMSO) & !is.na(dTag)),
    p_value = if (sum(!is.na(DMSO) & !is.na(dTag)) >= 2) {
      tryCatch(stats::t.test(DMSO, dTag, paired = TRUE)$p.value,
               error = function(e) NA_real_)
    } else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(test = "paired t-test (n = replicate pairs)")

# ---- QC: what is behind every bar and every test ---------------------------
qc <- occ_df %>%
  select(site_label, motif, read_set, Sample, occupancy,
         mean_depth, n_bp_used, acc_clusters) %>%
  left_join(
    calls_df %>%
      group_by(site_label, read_set, Sample) %>%
      summarise(n_reads_spanning      = dplyr::n(),
                pct_reads_footprinted = 100 * mean(footprinted == "yes"),
                .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("site_label", "read_set", "Sample")
  ) %>%
  arrange(site_label, read_set, Sample)
print(qc, n = Inf)

bind_rows(p_cmh      %>% select(site_label, read_set, p_value, test),
          p_paired_t %>% select(site_label, read_set, p_value, test)) %>%
  arrange(test, site_label, read_set) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r cmh-plot, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 3.5}
occ_mean <- occ_df %>%

# p-value label height: one per ROW, because facet_grid(scales = "free_y")
```
